title: Mikeitz

segments.he:
ענין זה הוא ענין בלבול והעלמת העיצה

״וְהִנֵּה מִן הַיְאֹר עֹלֹת שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת יְפוֹת מַרְאֶה וּבְרִיאֹת בָּשָׂר״ וְגוֹ׳ (מ״א, ב) כָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת הַעֲלָמַת הָעֵצָה, כִּי כָּל הָעֵצוֹת בְּכָל הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם כְּלוּלִים בְּשִׁבְעָה מִדּוֹת, שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לֵידַע אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּכָל מִדָּה. וְיֵשׁ עִתִּים שֶׁהַשּׁוֹנִי הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְאוֹר, הֵם מַעֲלִין כָּל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת כָּרָאוּי שֶׁהֵם טוֹבוֹת וְיָפוֹת בְּחִינַת בְּרִיאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת. אֲבָל בְּתוֹךְ כָּךְ מִתְגַּבֵּר הָרַע שֶׁהֵם הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת וּמְבַלְבְּלִין הַמֹּחַ עַד שֶׁבּוֹלְעִין כָּל הַטּוֹב, וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה כְּאִלּוּ מֵעוֹלָם לֹא הָיָה שָׁם טוֹב כְּלָל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.

וְאִם אַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים וּמְעוֹרְרִים הַטּוֹב בִּבְחִינַת שֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים מְלֵאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת. כִּי יֵשׁ טוֹב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר נֶפֶשׁ הַחַי שֶׁהוּא גָּבֹהַּ יוֹתֵר שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת טוֹבוֹת. וּכְשֶׁנִּתְבַּלְבֵּל עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבַע הַפָּרוֹת הָרָעוֹת חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב עַל כָּל פָּנִים בִּבְחִינַת בֵּרוּר הַצּוֹמֵחַ, שֶׁמְּרֻמָּז בְּשֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים מְלֵאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת. אֲבָל גַּם עַל זֶה חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַבִּלְבּוּלִים עַד שֶׁשֶּׁבַע הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הָרֵקוֹת וְהָרָעוֹת בּוֹלְעִים אוֹתָם.

וְכָל זֶה בְּחִינַת בִּלְבּוּל הָעֵצָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַפְּגָמִים, בְּחִינַת וַעֲצַת עֶלְיוֹן נָאָצוּ, וּכְתִיב וְהֵמָּה מָרוּ בַעֲצָתָם וַיִּמָּכְרוּ בַּעֲוֹנָם.

והתיקון לזה הוא על ידי הצדיק שמלמד עצות

וְהַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת שֶׁמִּתְיַגֵּעַ תָּמִיד לְהוֹסִיף בַּתּוֹרָה חִדּוּשִׁים נִפְלָאִים שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהֶם עֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף לֶקַח וְכוּ׳. בְּחִינַת הַמּוֹסִיף יוֹסִיף, בְּחִינַת מוֹסִיף וְהוֹלֵךְ. שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עֵצָה שֶׁיַּקְבִּצוּ אֶת הַטּוֹב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָאֹכֶל, שֶׁבַּשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁמַר הֵיטֵב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שֶׁעוֹסֵק לְזָרֵז לִכְתֹּב בַּסְּפָרִים כָּל חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה לְהַרְבּוֹת סְפָרִים עַד אֵין קֵץ שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקַּר שְׁמִירַת מַאֲכְלֵי הַתּוֹרָה. כִּי הַסֵּפֶר הוּא לְזִכָּרוֹן בְּחִינַת כְּתֹב זֹאת זִכָּרוֹן בַּסֵּפֶר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁמָר לְעוֹלָם וְלֹא יִהְיֶה נֶאֱבָד וְנִשְׁכָּח.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּר כְּחוֹל הַיָּם עַד כִּי חָדַל לִסְפֹּר כִּי אֵין מִסְפָּר, בְּחִינַת עֲשׂוֹת סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה אֵין קֵץ כִּי בְּיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, וְזָקֵן זֶה קָנָה חָכְמָה קָנָה בִּינָה. שֶׁמְּרֻמָּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין בּוֹ הַסְּפָרִים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה תִּהְיֶה עִקַּר הַגְּאֻלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בר״מ וּבְגָלוּתָא קַדְמָאָה בְּמַטֶּה דִּילָךְ בְּזַע יָמָא, וּבְגָלוּתָא בַּתְרָאָה בְּקָנֶה דִילָךְ דְּאִיהוּ קֻלְמָסָא בְּזַע יַמָּא דְאוֹרַיְתָא.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה כִּי הַמְּנוֹרָה הַטְּהוֹרָה זֶה בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעִקַּר קִיּוּמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַקָּנִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּסִים הַכּוֹתְבִים סִפְרֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעַל יָדָם עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁהוּא תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה.

וְיֵשׁ לְרַמֵּז שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ. בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קָנִים בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעַת קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּחִינַת כְּלַל הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנִים שֶׁכְּלוּלִים בְּשִׁבְעָה בְּחִינַת חָצְבָה עַמּוּדֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה, לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם כָּל חֲלֻקַּת הָעֵצָה לְבָרֵר הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים הַטּוֹבוֹת לְבָרְרָם מֵהַהֵפֶךְ הָרוֹצִים לְבַלְּעָם כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן מְרַמֵּז הַשֶּׁבַע הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הַתִּקּוּן אֵיךְ לְבָרְרָם שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים עֹלוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד בְּרִיאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד מְרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּס הַכּוֹתֶבֶת סִפְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן כַּנַּ״ל.

וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר, וּמוּבָא בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁהוּא חָבֵר לְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁיִּתְחַכְּמוּ דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר הַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנֶה תְּחַבֵּר אוֹתָם אֵלֶיךָ וּתְעַיֵּן בָּהֶם הֵיטֵב וְתוּכַל לֵידַע מִי הוּא הָרַב הָאֱמֶת. כִּי עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים כַּנַּ״ל.

(הלכות ראש חודש הלכה ו׳ אות י״ד)
segments.en:
This matter is the matter of the confusion and concealment of counsel.

“And behold, from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and healthy in flesh,” etc. (41:2). All this is the aspect of the concealment of counsel, for all counsels in all matters in the world are encompassed in seven attributes, and one must know how to conduct oneself in each attribute. And there are times when those who repeat halachos, who are the aspect of the river, raise all seven attributes properly, so that they are good and beautiful, the aspect of healthy and good. But meanwhile evil grows strong, which is the seven evil attributes, and they confuse the mind until they swallow all the good, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts,” as though there had never been any good there at all, God forbid.

And if afterward they return and gain strength and awaken the good in the aspect of seven full and good ears of grain—for there is good that is the aspect of refining the soul of the animal [level], which is higher, and this is the aspect of seven good cows—and when it becomes confused through the seven evil cows, they return and gain strength to refine the good at least in the aspect of refining the vegetable [level], which is alluded to in seven full and good ears of grain. But against this too the sitra achra and the confusions return and gain strength, until the seven empty and evil ears of grain swallow them.

And all this is the aspect of the confusion of counsel, from which all blemishes proceed, the aspect of “And they despised the counsel of the Most High,” and it is written, “And they rebelled through their counsel and were sold through their iniquity.”

And the rectification of this is through the tzaddik who teaches counsels.

And the rectification is through Yosef, who is the aspect of the true tzaddik, who always labors to add wondrous novel insights to the Torah, from which deep counsels proceed. This is the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of “he shall add learning,” etc.; the aspect of “he who adds shall increase,” the aspect of continually adding. He gives counsel that they gather the good, which is the aspect of the food, in the good years, so that it will be well preserved. This is the aspect of his occupying himself with urging that all novel Torah insights be written in books, multiplying books without end, which is the principal preservation of the foods of Torah. For the book is for remembrance, the aspect of “Write this as a remembrance in the book,” so that it will be preserved forever and will not be lost and forgotten.

And this is the aspect of “And Yosef amassed grain like the sand of the sea until he ceased counting, for there was no number,” the aspect of “making many books has no end.” For concerning Yosef it is said, “For he was a son of old age to him,” and “an elder”—one who has acquired wisdom, acquired understanding—which alludes to the reed and pen with which the books of the holy Torah are written, through which the principal redemption will come about. As stated in the holy Zohar, in Raaya Mehemna: “And in the first exile, with your staff split the sea, and in the final exile, with your reed, which is a pen, split the sea of Torah.”

And this is the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, for the pure Menorah is the aspect of the light of Torah, whose principal endurance is through the reeds, which are the aspect of the pens with which books of novel Torah insights are written; through them comes the principal rectification, which is the rectification of counsel.

And one may hint that this is the aspect of “for he was a son of old age to him”: the aspect of seven reeds, the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, the aspect of the totality of the holy books written with reeds, which are encompassed in seven, the aspect of “she has hewn her seven pillars,” to rectify all seven attributes in which all the divisions of counsel lie, to refine the seven good attributes, which are the seven good cows and the seven good ears of grain—to refine them from their opposite, which seeks to swallow them, as above. Therefore the seven ears of grain hint at the rectification, how to refine them: this is the aspect of “seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, healthy and good.” “On one stalk” alludes to the aforesaid reed, which is the aspect of the pen writing the books of Torah, etc., as above, through which the principal rectification comes, as above.

And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself and acquire a friend for yourself,” and it is cited in books that this alludes to the reed and pen, which is a friend to the Torah scholar, so that words of Torah become wiser through this. And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself”; and if he cannot find the rectification, [it is] through “and acquire a friend for yourself”: namely, through the holy books written with a reed—join them to yourself and study them carefully, and you will be able to know who is the true Rabbi. For the principal rectification is through multiplying books, as above.

(Halachos of Rosh Chodesh, Halacha 6, item 14)

All this is the aspect of the concealment of counsel, for all counsels in all matters in the world are encompassed in seven attributes, and one must know how to conduct oneself in each attribute. And there are times when those who repeat halachos, who are the aspect of the river, raise all seven attributes properly, so that they are good and beautiful, the aspect of healthy and good. But meanwhile evil grows strong, which is the seven evil attributes, and they confuse the mind until they swallow all the good, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts,” as though there had never been any good there at all, God forbid.

qualifiedAfter.en: “And behold, from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and healthy in flesh,” etc. (41:2). All this is the aspect of the concealment of counsel, for all counsels in all matters in the world are encompassed in seven attributes, and one must know how to conduct oneself in each attribute. And there are times when those who repeat halachos, who are the aspect of the river, raise all seven attributes properly, so that they are good and beautiful, the aspect of healthy and good. But meanwhile evil grows strong, which is the seven evil attributes, and they confuse the mind until they swallow all the good, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts,” as though there had never been any good there at all, God forbid.

pairs.he: וְאִם אַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים וּמְעוֹרְרִים הַטּוֹב בִּבְחִינַת שֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים מְלֵאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת. כִּי יֵשׁ טוֹב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר נֶפֶשׁ הַחַי שֶׁהוּא גָּבֹהַּ יוֹתֵר שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת טוֹבוֹת. וּכְשֶׁנִּתְבַּלְבֵּל עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבַע הַפָּרוֹת הָרָעוֹת חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב עַל כָּל פָּנִים בִּבְחִינַת בֵּרוּר הַצּוֹמֵחַ, שֶׁמְּרֻמָּז בְּשֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים מְלֵאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת. אֲבָל גַּם עַל זֶה חוֹזְרִים וּמִתְגַּבְּרִים הַסִּטְרָא אַחֲרָא וְהַבִּלְבּוּלִים עַד שֶׁשֶּׁבַע הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הָרֵקוֹת וְהָרָעוֹת בּוֹלְעִים אוֹתָם.
pairs.en: And if afterward they return and gain strength and awaken the good in the aspect of seven full and good ears of grain—for there is good that is the aspect of refining the soul of the animal [level], which is higher, and this is the aspect of seven good cows—and when it becomes confused through the seven evil cows, they return and gain strength to refine the good at least in the aspect of refining the vegetable [level], which is alluded to in seven full and good ears of grain. But against this too the sitra achra and the confusions return and gain strength, until the seven empty and evil ears of grain swallow them.

qualifiedAfter.en: And if afterward they return and gain strength and awaken the good in the aspect of seven full and good ears of grain—for there is good that is the aspect of refining the soul of the animal [level], which is higher, and this is the aspect of seven good cows—and when it becomes confused through the seven evil cows, they return and gain strength to refine the good at least in the aspect of refining the vegetable [level], which is alluded to in seven full and good ears of grain. But against this too the sitra achra and the confusions return and gain strength, until the seven empty and evil ears of grain swallow them.

pairs.he: וְכָל זֶה בְּחִינַת בִּלְבּוּל הָעֵצָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַפְּגָמִים, בְּחִינַת וַעֲצַת עֶלְיוֹן נָאָצוּ, וּכְתִיב וְהֵמָּה מָרוּ בַעֲצָתָם וַיִּמָּכְרוּ בַּעֲוֹנָם.
pairs.en: And all this is the aspect of the confusion of counsel, from which all blemishes proceed, the aspect of “And they despised the counsel of the Most High,” and it is written, “And they rebelled through their counsel and were sold through their iniquity.”

qualifiedAfter.en: And all this is the aspect of the confusion of counsel, from which all blemishes proceed, the aspect of “And they despised the counsel of the Most High,” and it is written, “And they rebelled through their counsel and were sold through their iniquity.”

pairs.he: והתיקון לזה הוא על ידי הצדיק שמלמד עצות
pairs.en: And the rectification of this is through the tzaddik who teaches counsels.

qualifiedAfter.he: והתיקון לזה הוא על ידי הצדיק שמלמד עצות
qualifiedAfter.en: And the rectification of this is through the tzaddik who teaches counsels.

pairs.he: וְהַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת שֶׁמִּתְיַגֵּעַ תָּמִיד לְהוֹסִיף בַּתּוֹרָה חִדּוּשִׁים נִפְלָאִים שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהֶם עֵצוֹת עֲמֻקּוֹת, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף לֶקַח וְכוּ׳. בְּחִינַת הַמּוֹסִיף יוֹסִיף, בְּחִינַת מוֹסִיף וְהוֹלֵךְ. שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עֵצָה שֶׁיַּקְבִּצוּ אֶת הַטּוֹב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָאֹכֶל, שֶׁבַּשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁמַר הֵיטֵב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שֶׁעוֹסֵק לְזָרֵז לִכְתֹּב בַּסְּפָרִים כָּל חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה לְהַרְבּוֹת סְפָרִים עַד אֵין קֵץ שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקַּר שְׁמִירַת מַאֲכְלֵי הַתּוֹרָה. כִּי הַסֵּפֶר הוּא לְזִכָּרוֹן בְּחִינַת כְּתֹב זֹאת זִכָּרוֹן בַּסֵּפֶר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁמָר לְעוֹלָם וְלֹא יִהְיֶה נֶאֱבָד וְנִשְׁכָּח.
pairs.en: And the rectification is through Yosef, who is the aspect of the true tzaddik, who always labors to add wondrous novel insights to the Torah, from which deep counsels proceed. This is the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of “he shall add learning,” etc.; the aspect of “he who adds shall increase,” the aspect of continually adding. He gives counsel that they gather the good, which is the aspect of the food, in the good years, so that it will be well preserved. This is the aspect of his occupying himself with urging that all novel Torah insights be written in books, multiplying books without end, which is the principal preservation of the foods of Torah. For the book is for remembrance, the aspect of “Write this as a remembrance in the book,” so that it will be preserved forever and will not be lost and forgotten.

qualifiedAfter.en: And the rectification is through Yosef, who is the aspect of the true tzaddik, who always labors to add wondrous novel insights to the Torah, from which deep counsels proceed. This is the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of “he shall add learning,” etc.; the aspect of “he who adds shall increase,” the aspect of continually adding. He gives counsel that they gather the good, which is the aspect of the food, in the good years, so that it will be well preserved. This is the aspect of his occupying himself with urging that all novel Torah insights be written in books, multiplying books without end, which is the principal preservation of the foods of Torah. For the book is for remembrance, the aspect of “Write this as a remembrance in the book,” so that it will be preserved forever and will not be lost and forgotten.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּר כְּחוֹל הַיָּם עַד כִּי חָדַל לִסְפֹּר כִּי אֵין מִסְפָּר, בְּחִינַת עֲשׂוֹת סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה אֵין קֵץ כִּי בְּיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, וְזָקֵן זֶה קָנָה חָכְמָה קָנָה בִּינָה. שֶׁמְּרֻמָּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין בּוֹ הַסְּפָרִים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה תִּהְיֶה עִקַּר הַגְּאֻלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בר״מ וּבְגָלוּתָא קַדְמָאָה בְּמַטֶּה דִּילָךְ בְּזַע יָמָא, וּבְגָלוּתָא בַּתְרָאָה בְּקָנֶה דִילָךְ דְּאִיהוּ קֻלְמָסָא בְּזַע יַמָּא דְאוֹרַיְתָא.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of “And Yosef amassed grain like the sand of the sea until he ceased counting, for there was no number,” the aspect of “making many books has no end.” For concerning Yosef it is said, “For he was a son of old age to him,” and “an elder”—one who has acquired wisdom, acquired understanding—which alludes to the reed and pen with which the books of the holy Torah are written, through which the principal redemption will come about. As stated in the holy Zohar, in Raaya Mehemna: “And in the first exile, with your staff split the sea, and in the final exile, with your reed, which is a pen, split the sea of Torah.”

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה כִּי הַמְּנוֹרָה הַטְּהוֹרָה זֶה בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעִקַּר קִיּוּמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַקָּנִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּסִים הַכּוֹתְבִים סִפְרֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעַל יָדָם עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁהוּא תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, for the pure Menorah is the aspect of the light of Torah, whose principal endurance is through the reeds, which are the aspect of the pens with which books of novel Torah insights are written; through them comes the principal rectification, which is the rectification of counsel.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, for the pure Menorah is the aspect of the light of Torah, whose principal endurance is through the reeds, which are the aspect of the pens with which books of novel Torah insights are written; through them comes the principal rectification, which is the rectification of counsel.

pairs.he: וְיֵשׁ לְרַמֵּז שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ. בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קָנִים בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעַת קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּחִינַת כְּלַל הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנִים שֶׁכְּלוּלִים בְּשִׁבְעָה בְּחִינַת חָצְבָה עַמּוּדֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה, לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם כָּל חֲלֻקַּת הָעֵצָה לְבָרֵר הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים הַטּוֹבוֹת לְבָרְרָם מֵהַהֵפֶךְ הָרוֹצִים לְבַלְּעָם כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן מְרַמֵּז הַשֶּׁבַע הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הַתִּקּוּן אֵיךְ לְבָרְרָם שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים עֹלוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד בְּרִיאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד מְרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּס הַכּוֹתֶבֶת סִפְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And one may hint that this is the aspect of “for he was a son of old age to him”: the aspect of seven reeds, the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, the aspect of the totality of the holy books written with reeds, which are encompassed in seven, the aspect of “she has hewn her seven pillars,” to rectify all seven attributes in which all the divisions of counsel lie, to refine the seven good attributes, which are the seven good cows and the seven good ears of grain—to refine them from their opposite, which seeks to swallow them, as above. Therefore the seven ears of grain hint at the rectification, how to refine them: this is the aspect of “seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, healthy and good.” “On one stalk” alludes to the aforesaid reed, which is the aspect of the pen writing the books of Torah, etc., as above, through which the principal rectification comes, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And one may hint that this is the aspect of “for he was a son of old age to him”: the aspect of seven reeds, the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, the aspect of the totality of the holy books written with reeds, which are encompassed in seven, the aspect of “she has hewn her seven pillars,” to rectify all seven attributes in which all the divisions of counsel lie, to refine the seven good attributes, which are the seven good cows and the seven good ears of grain—to refine them from their opposite, which seeks to swallow them, as above. Therefore the seven ears of grain hint at the rectification, how to refine them: this is the aspect of “seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, healthy and good.” “On one stalk” alludes to the aforesaid reed, which is the aspect of the pen writing the books of Torah, etc., as above, through which the principal rectification comes, as above.

pairs.he: וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר, וּמוּבָא בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁהוּא חָבֵר לְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁיִּתְחַכְּמוּ דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר הַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנֶה תְּחַבֵּר אוֹתָם אֵלֶיךָ וּתְעַיֵּן בָּהֶם הֵיטֵב וְתוּכַל לֵידַע מִי הוּא הָרַב הָאֱמֶת. כִּי עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself and acquire a friend for yourself,” and it is cited in books that this alludes to the reed and pen, which is a friend to the Torah scholar, so that words of Torah become wiser through this. And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself”; and if he cannot find the rectification, [it is] through “and acquire a friend for yourself”: namely, through the holy books written with a reed—join them to yourself and study them carefully, and you will be able to know who is the true Rabbi. For the principal rectification is through multiplying books, as above.

הוא ענין התגברות כח המדמה והשכחה

״וְהִנֵּה מִן הַיְאֹר עֹלֹת שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת יְפוֹת מַרְאֶה וּבְרִיאֹת בָּשָׂר״ וְגוֹ׳ (מ״א, ב) עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ הַמְּדַבֵּר מִשְּׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן בְּלִקּוּטֵי הָרִאשׁוֹן סִימָן נד, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵרֹאשׁוֹ לְסוֹפוֹ.

וְהַכְּלָל כִּי צְרִיכִין לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד אֶת הַזִּכָּרוֹן, הַיְנוּ לְאַדְבְּקָא מַחֲשַׁבְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי לִזְכֹּר תָּמִיד בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ אֶת עוֹלָם הַנִּצְחִי שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְלֹא יִפֹּל לְשִׁכְחָה שֶׁהוּא מִיתַת הַלֵּב, שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח אֶת עוֹלָם הַבָּא כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו וּשְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן הוּא בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם מַה שֶּׁמְּבֹאָר עַל פָּסוּק ה׳ אֱלֹקַי גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד וְכוּ׳. וְאֵצֶל הֲמוֹן עַם נַעֲשֶׂה כָּל זֶה מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי שֵׁנָה וְצִיצִית וּתְפִלִּין וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּתְפִלָּה וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן, עַיֵּן שָׁם.

וּמְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כָּל הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד צַדִּיק וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נוֹטֶה שָׁמַיִם כַּיְרִיעָה, כִּי בְּכָל הַדְּבָרִים יֵשׁ נִיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים וְעַל יְדֵי הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן נִתְחַבְּרִין וְנִתְעַלִּין הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת כְּפִי חֶלְקֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד צַדִּיק וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַיֵּן שָׁם הֵיטֵב. וְלִשְׁמֹר הַזִּכָּרוֹן צְרִיכִין לִשְׁמֹר עַצְמוֹ מֵרַע עַיִן וְכוּ׳ גַּם צְרִיכִים לִשְׁמֹר עַצְמוֹ מִכֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פַּרְעֹה וְכוּ׳ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.

וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, בְּחִינַת עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְעֹה בְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי פַּרְעֹה הוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה, בְּחִינַת פְּגַם הַזִּכָּרוֹן בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, כַּמְבֹאָר שָׁם, וְעַל כֵּן רָצָה לְהַגְבִּיר בְּחִינַת הָעַבְדוּת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּדֵי לְהַפִּיל עֲלֵיהֶם שִׁכְחָה כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לְאַדְבֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי נִרְפִּים הֵם עַל כֵּן הֵם צוֹעֲקִים לֵאמֹר נֵלְכָה וְנִזְבְּחָה לֵאלֹקֵינוּ תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבוֹדָה וְיַעֲשׂוּ בָהּ וְאַל יִשְׁעוּ וְכוּ׳.

וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִבְטִיחַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּגָלוּת בִּבְחִינַת עַבְדוּת אֵצֶל פַּרְעֹה שֶׁכָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, כִּי זֶה הָעֲשִׁירוּת הַגָּדוֹל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁזָּכוּ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר נִיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מִן הַקְּלִפּוֹת קלד שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַזִּכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְתַּקֵּן פְּגַם הָעַבְדוּת וְהַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וְכַנַּ״ל.

וּפָרָה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, כִּי עִקַּר הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא מִבְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל, וְעִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא בִּבְחִינַת פָּרָה בְּיוֹתֵר, כִּי הִיא עִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כִּי מֶלֶךְ שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שׁוֹר (חגיגה דף י״ג ע״ב) וְכָל הַבְּהֵמוֹת כְּלוּלִים בּוֹ וְעִקַּר אֲחִיזַת הַשִּׁכְחָה בִּבְחִינַת בַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּנַּ״ל.

וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ, כִּי דְּכוּרָא נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם זָכוֹר, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמִּשָּׁם בְּחִינַת זִכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בַּבְּהֵמוֹת נֶאֱחָז הַשִּׁכְחָה בְּיוֹתֵר בִּבְחִינַת הַנּוּקְבָא שֶׁל הַשּׁוֹר שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ וְהַכְּלָל שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁהִיא הַפָּרָה. וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא הַשַּׂר שֶׁל שִׁכְחָה פּוּרָה, עַל שֵׁם פָּרָה כּמובא קלה.

וְזֶה כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִים אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְסָרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ כְּתִיב כִּי כְּפָרָה סוֹרֵרָה סָרַר יִשְׂרָאֵל.

וְעַל כֵּן פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה כֹּחַ הַבַּטֵּל כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל וְרָצָה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַמְשִׁיכָם לְגָלוּת וְעַבְדוּת תַּחַת יָדוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶת הַזִּכָּרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִים לְדַבֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם שָׁם, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁהֵם הִתְחִילוּ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ זֶה הַזִּכָּרוֹן בָּעוֹלָם כִּי הֵם הוֹדִיעוּ וְגִלּוּ אֱלֹקוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם (וכמבואר מזה במקום אחר).

עַל כֵּן רָאָה פַּרְעֹה בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא, שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת רָעוֹת וְשֶׁאָכְלוּ הַפָּרוֹת הָרָעוֹת אֶת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה, שֶׁכָּל זֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁיִּתְגַּבֵּר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָרַע עַל הַטּוֹב עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁכַּח הַטּוֹב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת וְנִשְׁכַּח כָּל הַשָּׂבָע וְכוּ׳. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה חֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא כִּי שָׁם עִקַּר אֲחִיזַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פָּרָה כַּנַּ״ל.

אֲבָל הַתִּקּוּן הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף, כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּתַר יוֹסֵף אֶת הַחֲלוֹם לְפַרְעֹה וְנַעֲשָׂה מֶלֶךְ וְקִבֵּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁבַר וּבִטֵּל אֶת הָרָעָב וְהִגְבִּיר הַטּוֹב עַל הָרַע, וְעַל יְדֵי קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ הִכְנִיעַ הַזֻּהֲמָא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָצֵאת מִשָּׁם. כִּי עִקַּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בְּכֹחַ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.

כִּי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן, הוּא מַכְנִיעַ בְּחִינַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וּמְבָרֵר הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִן הַשִּׁכְחָה, וְעַל כֵּן הוּא יוֹדֵעַ לִפְתֹּר הַחֲלוֹם שֶׁל הַפָּרוֹת וּלְהַכְנִיעַ וּלְבַטֵּל הַשִּׁכְחָה הַנֶּאֱחָז בָּהֶם שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב, כִּי הוּא מַגְבִּיר הַשָּׂבָע עַל הָרָעָב וּמַמְשִׁיךְ כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת וְהַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.

(הלכות שוכר הלכה ג׳)
segments.en:
It is the matter of the ascendency of the imaginative faculty and forgetfulness.

“And behold, from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and healthy in flesh,” etc. (41:2), according to the teaching “And it was at the end,” which discusses preserving memory, in Likutay, the first [collection], section 54; see there the entire teaching from its beginning to its end.

And the principle is that one must guard memory very carefully: namely, to attach thought to the world to come, constantly remembering in his thought the eternal world, which is the world to come, and not fall into forgetfulness, which is the death of the heart, so that he not forget the world to come throughout all the days of his life. Preserving memory is in general and in particular, etc.; see there what is explained concerning the verse “Hashem my God, You are very great,” etc. And among the general populace all this comes about of itself through sleep and tzitzis and tefillin, the recitation of Shema, prayer and commerce; see there.

And it is explained there that through all commerce a unification of the tzaddik and the Congregation of Israel is made, which is the aspect of “stretching the heavens like a curtain.” For in all things there are holy sparks, and through commerce the sparks become joined and elevated according to the portions of nefesh, ru’ach and neshamah that each person has; through this a unification of the tzaddik and the Congregation of Israel is made; see there carefully. To preserve memory one must guard oneself from an evil eye, etc.; one must also guard oneself from the imaginative faculty, which is the aspect of Pharaoh, etc., etc.; see all this there carefully.

And this is the aspect of the exile in Egypt, the aspect of “We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt,” for Pharaoh is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of the blemish in memory, the aspect of forgetfulness, as explained there. Therefore he wanted to strengthen the aspect of servitude over Israel, to cast forgetfulness upon them so that they could not attach their thought to the world to come, as it is written, “For they are idle; therefore they cry out, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God. Let the work be heavy, and let them labor in it, and let them not turn,” etc.

And this is the aspect of what Hashem, blessed be He, promised Avraham our forefather: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” That is, He promised him that although they would be in exile in the aspect of servitude with Pharaoh, all of which is the aspect of forgetfulness, afterward they would go out with great possessions. For this great wealth of holiness that they merited in the Exodus from Egypt is the aspect of refining holy sparks from the klipos [printed note marker: 134], which is the aspect of rectifying memory. Therefore through this the blemish of servitude and exile, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, was rectified, as above.

And a cow is the aspect of forgetfulness, for forgetfulness principally comes from the aspect of the imaginative faculty, which is the power of animality, as explained in the aforesaid teaching. The chief animality and forgetfulness are particularly in the aspect of a cow, for she is the principal animality, for “the king among the animals is the ox” (Chagigah, folio 13b)—and all the animals are encompassed in it, and forgetfulness principally takes hold in the aspect of animality, as above.

And forgetfulness is from the feminine side, as is known, for the masculine is named after “remember,” because from there is the aspect of memory. Therefore even among the animals forgetfulness takes hold particularly in the aspect of the female of the ox, which is the head and totality among the animals, namely the cow. Therefore the minister of forgetfulness is called Purah, after parah, a cow, as cited [printed note marker: 135].

And this is that when Israel are reproved for having forgotten Hashem, blessed be He, and turned away from Him, it is written, “For like a rebellious cow, Israel rebelled.”

And therefore Pharaoh, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the idle faculty, as explained in the aforesaid teaching, wanted to prevail over Israel and draw them into exile and servitude under his hand, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, to make them forget, God forbid, the remembrance of the world to come, to which they were accustomed to attach their thought, according to what they received from their forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who began to draw this remembrance into the world, for they made known and revealed His divinity in the world (as explained concerning this elsewhere).

Therefore Pharaoh saw cows specifically in his dream: seven good cows and seven evil cows, and the evil cows ate the good ones, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts.” All this indicates that evil would prevail over good, God forbid, until good is forgotten, God forbid, in the aspect of “and all the plenty shall be forgotten,” etc. Therefore his dream was specifically cows, for there Pharaoh principally takes hold, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of forgetfulness, which is the aspect of a cow, as above.

But the rectification was through Yosef, for through Yosef interpreting the dream for Pharaoh and becoming king and gathering all the food of the seven good years, through this he broke and annulled the famine and strengthened good over evil; and through his holiness he subdued the pollution of Egypt, and through this Israel merited to leave there. For the Exodus from Egypt was principally through the power of Yosef the tzaddik, as it is written, “And Moshe took Yosef’s bones with him,” as stated in the holy Zohar.

For Yosef, who is the aspect of preserving memory, subdues the aspect of Pharaoh, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, and refines memory out of forgetfulness. Therefore he knows how to interpret the dream of the cows and subdue and annul the forgetfulness that takes hold in them, which is the seven years of famine, for he strengthens plenty over famine and draws all beneficence and blessings through preserving memory, from which all blessings proceed, as above.

(Halachos of Hiring, Halacha 3)

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִבְטִיחַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּגָלוּת בִּבְחִינַת עַבְדוּת אֵצֶל פַּרְעֹה שֶׁכָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, כִּי זֶה הָעֲשִׁירוּת הַגָּדוֹל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁזָּכוּ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר נִיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מִן הַקְּלִפּוֹת קלד שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַזִּכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְתַּקֵּן פְּגַם הָעַבְדוּת וְהַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of what Hashem, blessed be He, promised Avraham our forefather: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” That is, He promised him that although they would be in exile in the aspect of servitude with Pharaoh, all of which is the aspect of forgetfulness, afterward they would go out with great possessions. For this great wealth of holiness that they merited in the Exodus from Egypt is the aspect of refining holy sparks from the klipos [printed note marker: 134], which is the aspect of rectifying memory. Therefore through this the blemish of servitude and exile, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, was rectified, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of what Hashem, blessed be He, promised Avraham our forefather: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” That is, He promised him that although they would be in exile in the aspect of servitude with Pharaoh, all of which is the aspect of forgetfulness, afterward they would go out with great possessions. For this great wealth of holiness that they merited in the Exodus from Egypt is the aspect of refining holy sparks from the klipos [printed note marker: 134], which is the aspect of rectifying memory. Therefore through this the blemish of servitude and exile, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, was rectified, as above.

pairs.he: וּפָרָה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, כִּי עִקַּר הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא מִבְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל, וְעִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא בִּבְחִינַת פָּרָה בְּיוֹתֵר, כִּי הִיא עִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כִּי מֶלֶךְ שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שׁוֹר (חגיגה דף י״ג ע״ב) וְכָל הַבְּהֵמוֹת כְּלוּלִים בּוֹ וְעִקַּר אֲחִיזַת הַשִּׁכְחָה בִּבְחִינַת בַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And a cow is the aspect of forgetfulness, for forgetfulness principally comes from the aspect of the imaginative faculty, which is the power of animality, as explained in the aforesaid teaching. The chief animality and forgetfulness are particularly in the aspect of a cow, for she is the principal animality, for “the king among the animals is the ox” (Chagigah, folio 13b)—and all the animals are encompassed in it, and forgetfulness principally takes hold in the aspect of animality, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And a cow is the aspect of forgetfulness, for forgetfulness principally comes from the aspect of the imaginative faculty, which is the power of animality, as explained in the aforesaid teaching. The chief animality and forgetfulness are particularly in the aspect of a cow, for she is the principal animality, for “the king among the animals is the ox” (Chagigah, folio 13b)—and all the animals are encompassed in it, and forgetfulness principally takes hold in the aspect of animality, as above.

pairs.he: וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ, כִּי דְּכוּרָא נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם זָכוֹר, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמִּשָּׁם בְּחִינַת זִכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בַּבְּהֵמוֹת נֶאֱחָז הַשִּׁכְחָה בְּיוֹתֵר בִּבְחִינַת הַנּוּקְבָא שֶׁל הַשּׁוֹר שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ וְהַכְּלָל שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁהִיא הַפָּרָה. וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא הַשַּׂר שֶׁל שִׁכְחָה פּוּרָה, עַל שֵׁם פָּרָה כּמובא קלה.
pairs.en: And forgetfulness is from the feminine side, as is known, for the masculine is named after “remember,” because from there is the aspect of memory. Therefore even among the animals forgetfulness takes hold particularly in the aspect of the female of the ox, which is the head and totality among the animals, namely the cow. Therefore the minister of forgetfulness is called Purah, after parah, a cow, as cited [printed note marker: 135].

qualifiedAfter.en: And forgetfulness is from the feminine side, as is known, for the masculine is named after “remember,” because from there is the aspect of memory. Therefore even among the animals forgetfulness takes hold particularly in the aspect of the female of the ox, which is the head and totality among the animals, namely the cow. Therefore the minister of forgetfulness is called Purah, after parah, a cow, as cited [printed note marker: 135].

pairs.he: וְזֶה כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִים אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְסָרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ כְּתִיב כִּי כְּפָרָה סוֹרֵרָה סָרַר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
pairs.en: And this is that when Israel are reproved for having forgotten Hashem, blessed be He, and turned away from Him, it is written, “For like a rebellious cow, Israel rebelled.”

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is that when Israel are reproved for having forgotten Hashem, blessed be He, and turned away from Him, it is written, “For like a rebellious cow, Israel rebelled.”

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה כֹּחַ הַבַּטֵּל כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל וְרָצָה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַמְשִׁיכָם לְגָלוּת וְעַבְדוּת תַּחַת יָדוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶת הַזִּכָּרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִים לְדַבֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם שָׁם, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁהֵם הִתְחִילוּ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ זֶה הַזִּכָּרוֹן בָּעוֹלָם כִּי הֵם הוֹדִיעוּ וְגִלּוּ אֱלֹקוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם (וכמבואר מזה במקום אחר).
pairs.en: And therefore Pharaoh, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the idle faculty, as explained in the aforesaid teaching, wanted to prevail over Israel and draw them into exile and servitude under his hand, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, to make them forget, God forbid, the remembrance of the world to come, to which they were accustomed to attach their thought, according to what they received from their forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who began to draw this remembrance into the world, for they made known and revealed His divinity in the world (as explained concerning this elsewhere).

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore Pharaoh, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the idle faculty, as explained in the aforesaid teaching, wanted to prevail over Israel and draw them into exile and servitude under his hand, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, to make them forget, God forbid, the remembrance of the world to come, to which they were accustomed to attach their thought, according to what they received from their forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who began to draw this remembrance into the world, for they made known and revealed His divinity in the world (as explained concerning this elsewhere).

pairs.he: עַל כֵּן רָאָה פַּרְעֹה בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא, שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת רָעוֹת וְשֶׁאָכְלוּ הַפָּרוֹת הָרָעוֹת אֶת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה, שֶׁכָּל זֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁיִּתְגַּבֵּר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָרַע עַל הַטּוֹב עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁכַּח הַטּוֹב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת וְנִשְׁכַּח כָּל הַשָּׂבָע וְכוּ׳. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה חֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא כִּי שָׁם עִקַּר אֲחִיזַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פָּרָה כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: Therefore Pharaoh saw cows specifically in his dream: seven good cows and seven evil cows, and the evil cows ate the good ones, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts.” All this indicates that evil would prevail over good, God forbid, until good is forgotten, God forbid, in the aspect of “and all the plenty shall be forgotten,” etc. Therefore his dream was specifically cows, for there Pharaoh principally takes hold, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of forgetfulness, which is the aspect of a cow, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: Therefore Pharaoh saw cows specifically in his dream: seven good cows and seven evil cows, and the evil cows ate the good ones, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts.” All this indicates that evil would prevail over good, God forbid, until good is forgotten, God forbid, in the aspect of “and all the plenty shall be forgotten,” etc. Therefore his dream was specifically cows, for there Pharaoh principally takes hold, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of forgetfulness, which is the aspect of a cow, as above.

pairs.he: אֲבָל הַתִּקּוּן הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף, כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּתַר יוֹסֵף אֶת הַחֲלוֹם לְפַרְעֹה וְנַעֲשָׂה מֶלֶךְ וְקִבֵּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁבַר וּבִטֵּל אֶת הָרָעָב וְהִגְבִּיר הַטּוֹב עַל הָרַע, וְעַל יְדֵי קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ הִכְנִיעַ הַזֻּהֲמָא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָצֵאת מִשָּׁם. כִּי עִקַּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בְּכֹחַ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
pairs.en: But the rectification was through Yosef, for through Yosef interpreting the dream for Pharaoh and becoming king and gathering all the food of the seven good years, through this he broke and annulled the famine and strengthened good over evil; and through his holiness he subdued the pollution of Egypt, and through this Israel merited to leave there. For the Exodus from Egypt was principally through the power of Yosef the tzaddik, as it is written, “And Moshe took Yosef’s bones with him,” as stated in the holy Zohar.

qualifiedAfter.en: But the rectification was through Yosef, for through Yosef interpreting the dream for Pharaoh and becoming king and gathering all the food of the seven good years, through this he broke and annulled the famine and strengthened good over evil; and through his holiness he subdued the pollution of Egypt, and through this Israel merited to leave there. For the Exodus from Egypt was principally through the power of Yosef the tzaddik, as it is written, “And Moshe took Yosef’s bones with him,” as stated in the holy Zohar.

pairs.he: כִּי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן, הוּא מַכְנִיעַ בְּחִינַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וּמְבָרֵר הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִן הַשִּׁכְחָה, וְעַל כֵּן הוּא יוֹדֵעַ לִפְתֹּר הַחֲלוֹם שֶׁל הַפָּרוֹת וּלְהַכְנִיעַ וּלְבַטֵּל הַשִּׁכְחָה הַנֶּאֱחָז בָּהֶם שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב, כִּי הוּא מַגְבִּיר הַשָּׂבָע עַל הָרָעָב וּמַמְשִׁיךְ כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת וְהַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: For Yosef, who is the aspect of preserving memory, subdues the aspect of Pharaoh, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, and refines memory out of forgetfulness. Therefore he knows how to interpret the dream of the cows and subdue and annul the forgetfulness that takes hold in them, which is the seven years of famine, for he strengthens plenty over famine and draws all beneficence and blessings through preserving memory, from which all blessings proceed, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: For Yosef, who is the aspect of preserving memory, subdues the aspect of Pharaoh, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, and refines memory out of forgetfulness. Therefore he knows how to interpret the dream of the cows and subdue and annul the forgetfulness that takes hold in them, which is the seven years of famine, for he strengthens plenty over famine and draws all beneficence and blessings through preserving memory, from which all blessings proceed, as above.

קלד.

מפורסם זה בספה״ק, כגון הבאר מים חיים (בתחילת פרשת וישב): שיעקב ובניו ירדו מצרימה הכל היה לפי שהם תולדות יעקב והוא קיבל עליו ועל זרעו אחריו להיות גרים בארץ לא להם ועבדום וענו אותם בכדי לצאת ברכוש גדול, להוציא כל ניצוצות של הקדושה שהיו מוטבעים במעמקי קליפת מצרים לקחת בלעם מפיהם להיות חיל בלע ויקיאנו. ע״כ. וכן בזרע קודש בפרשת בא (דבר נא וגו׳) וז״ל: כדי שלא יאמר אותו צדיק וכו׳ ואחרי כן יצאו ברכוש גדול לא קיים בהם. על זה יש לתמוה וכי חשוד אותו צדיק אברהם ע״ה שיתרעם וכו׳, ועוד, וכי היה אברהם מבקש רכוש של ממון אדרבא היה שונא רכוש כמו שמצינו במלחמת ד׳ מלכים וכו׳. והנה גלות מצרים היה עיקר הכונה שיוציאו ישראל משם כל ניצוצות הקדושות שנפלו בקליפה כמבואר כמה פעמים בזוה״ק שזה הוא עיקר הרכוש הפנימי אשר הוציאו ישראל ממצרים. ע״כ. ועוד טובא.
segments.en:
134.

This is well known in the holy books, for example B’ear Mayim Chayim (at the beginning of the parsha Vayeishev): That Yaakov and his sons went down to Egypt—all of it was because they were the descendants of Yaakov, and he accepted upon himself and upon his seed after him that they should be strangers in a land not theirs, “and they will enslave them and afflict them,” in order to go out with great wealth: to bring out all the sparks of holiness that were embedded in the depths of the klipah of Egypt, to take what they had swallowed out of their mouths, so that “He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out.” Thus far. And likewise in Zera Kodesh in the parsha Bo (“Speak, please,” etc.), and these are its words: So that that righteous man should not say, etc., “and afterward they will go out with great wealth” He did not fulfill for them. Concerning this one must wonder: Is that righteous man Avraham, peace be upon him, suspected of complaining, etc.? And furthermore, was Avraham seeking monetary wealth? On the contrary, he hated wealth, as we find in the war of the four kings, etc. And behold, the principal intention of the Egyptian exile was that Israel should bring out from there all the holy sparks that had fallen into the klipah, as is explained many times in the holy Zohar, that this is the principal inward wealth that Israel brought out of Egypt. Thus far. And much more besides.

segments.he:
יוסף נותן עצה שישמור את זמני ההתעוררות לזמנים הקשים שיבואו

״וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן״ וְגוֹ׳ ״וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב״ (מ״א, לו) זֶה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁל חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה, שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עֵצָה שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם הַשִּׂבְעָה וְהַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמֹּחִין שֶׁל חוּץ לָאָרֶץ.

וַעֲצָתוֹ הוּא שֶׁיִּקְבְּצוּ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטֹּבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר עַל הָאָדָם אֵיזֶה טוֹב בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת, אָז תֵּכֶף יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה עֻבְדָּא דִקְדֻשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתוֹ, לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אוֹ לִלְמֹד אוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה, וְיַעֲשֶׂה לְעַצְמוֹ אוֹצָרוֹת בְּמֹחוֹ לְהַטְמִין שָׁם אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, כִּי הָאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּחִירָה וְיֵשׁ כֹּחַ בְּיָדוֹ כְּשֶׁבָּא עָלָיו אֵיזֶה תְּשׁוּקָה טוֹבָה, לְהַטְמִין וּלְקַשֵּׁר אוֹתָהּ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ וְלִקַּח בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ זֹאת הַתְּשׁוּקָה לְזָכְרָהּ הֵיטֵב שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכָּחֶנָּה.

כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק מוֹדִיעַ לוֹ מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יָבוֹאוּ עָלָיו יְמֵי רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְיִרְצוּ לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל הַטּוֹב הַהוּא, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין מֵעַצְמוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִגְנֹז הֵיטֵב אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיְּקַשֵּׁר הַחֵשֶׁק דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְיִקַּח בְּדַעְתּוֹ זֶה הָעִנְיָן בְּעַצְמוֹ. שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁיִּטַּמְטֵם לִבּוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָרַע שֶׁבַּחוֹבְלִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יִתְחַזֵּק בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה׳ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַתְּשׁוּקָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְכָל הָרְשִׁימוֹת שֶׁל הַתְּשׁוּקוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ יִהְיוּ לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ בִּימֵי רַע שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. בִּבְחִינַת וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן לָאָרֶץ לְשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב אֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶינָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן. וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב כַּנַּ״ל.

(הלכות ברכת הפירות הלכה ד׳ אות י״ב)
segments.en:
Yosef gives counsel that one preserve the times of awakening for the difficult times that will come.

“And the food shall be for a deposit,” etc., “and the land shall not be cut off through famine” (41:36). This is the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of the rectification of Pharaoh’s dream, who gives counsel so that the satiation and good of the seven years of plenty will endure, and the land will not be cut off through famine, which is the aspect of the mental faculties of outside the Land.

And his counsel is that they gather all the food of these seven good years, “and the food shall be for a deposit,” etc. That is, immediately when some good awakens upon a person, the aspect of the holiness of the Land of Israel, from which all sanctities proceed, he should immediately perform some holy deed through his yearning: pray or study or perform some mitzvah. And he should make storehouses for himself in his mind, to hide there all the good of the seven good years. For a person has free choice, and he has the power, when some good yearning comes upon him, to conceal and bind it in the inwardness of his mind and take this yearning into his thought, to remember it well so that he will not forget it.

For since Yosef the tzaddik informs him beforehand that afterward days of evil will come upon him, God forbid, and will seek to make him forget all that good, through this the discerning person will understand on his own that he must carefully store away all the good of the aspect of the seven years of plenty. That is, he should bind the holy desire in his thought and take this very matter into his awareness: even when his heart becomes stopped up through the awakening of evil in the destroyers, nevertheless he should strengthen himself in the service of Hashem by reminding himself of the first yearning, as above. And all the impressions of the first yearnings that he stored in the inwardness of his mind will be for him a deposit to revive his soul in days of evil, which are the aspect of the seven years of famine; in the aspect of “And the food shall be for a deposit for the land for the seven years of famine that will come afterward, and the land shall not be cut off through famine,” as above.

(Halachos of the Blessing on Fruits, Halacha 4, item 12)

pairs.he: ״וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן״ וְגוֹ׳ ״וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב״ (מ״א, לו) זֶה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁל חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה, שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עֵצָה שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם הַשִּׂבְעָה וְהַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמֹּחִין שֶׁל חוּץ לָאָרֶץ.
pairs.en: “And the food shall be for a deposit,” etc., “and the land shall not be cut off through famine” (41:36). This is the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of the rectification of Pharaoh’s dream, who gives counsel so that the satiation and good of the seven years of plenty will endure, and the land will not be cut off through famine, which is the aspect of the mental faculties of outside the Land.

qualifiedAfter.en: “And the food shall be for a deposit,” etc., “and the land shall not be cut off through famine” (41:36). This is the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of the rectification of Pharaoh’s dream, who gives counsel so that the satiation and good of the seven years of plenty will endure, and the land will not be cut off through famine, which is the aspect of the mental faculties of outside the Land.

pairs.he: וַעֲצָתוֹ הוּא שֶׁיִּקְבְּצוּ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטֹּבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר עַל הָאָדָם אֵיזֶה טוֹב בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת, אָז תֵּכֶף יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה עֻבְדָּא דִקְדֻשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתוֹ, לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אוֹ לִלְמֹד אוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה, וְיַעֲשֶׂה לְעַצְמוֹ אוֹצָרוֹת בְּמֹחוֹ לְהַטְמִין שָׁם אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, כִּי הָאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּחִירָה וְיֵשׁ כֹּחַ בְּיָדוֹ כְּשֶׁבָּא עָלָיו אֵיזֶה תְּשׁוּקָה טוֹבָה, לְהַטְמִין וּלְקַשֵּׁר אוֹתָהּ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ וְלִקַּח בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ זֹאת הַתְּשׁוּקָה לְזָכְרָהּ הֵיטֵב שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכָּחֶנָּה.
pairs.en: And his counsel is that they gather all the food of these seven good years, “and the food shall be for a deposit,” etc. That is, immediately when some good awakens upon a person, the aspect of the holiness of the Land of Israel, from which all sanctities proceed, he should immediately perform some holy deed through his yearning: pray or study or perform some mitzvah. And he should make storehouses for himself in his mind, to hide there all the good of the seven good years. For a person has free choice, and he has the power, when some good yearning comes upon him, to conceal and bind it in the inwardness of his mind and take this yearning into his thought, to remember it well so that he will not forget it.

qualifiedAfter.en: And his counsel is that they gather all the food of these seven good years, “and the food shall be for a deposit,” etc. That is, immediately when some good awakens upon a person, the aspect of the holiness of the Land of Israel, from which all sanctities proceed, he should immediately perform some holy deed through his yearning: pray or study or perform some mitzvah. And he should make storehouses for himself in his mind, to hide there all the good of the seven good years. For a person has free choice, and he has the power, when some good yearning comes upon him, to conceal and bind it in the inwardness of his mind and take this yearning into his thought, to remember it well so that he will not forget it.

pairs.he: כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק מוֹדִיעַ לוֹ מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יָבוֹאוּ עָלָיו יְמֵי רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְיִרְצוּ לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל הַטּוֹב הַהוּא, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין מֵעַצְמוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִגְנֹז הֵיטֵב אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיְּקַשֵּׁר הַחֵשֶׁק דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְיִקַּח בְּדַעְתּוֹ זֶה הָעִנְיָן בְּעַצְמוֹ. שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁיִּטַּמְטֵם לִבּוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָרַע שֶׁבַּחוֹבְלִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יִתְחַזֵּק בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה׳ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַתְּשׁוּקָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְכָל הָרְשִׁימוֹת שֶׁל הַתְּשׁוּקוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ יִהְיוּ לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ בִּימֵי רַע שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. בִּבְחִינַת וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן לָאָרֶץ לְשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב אֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶינָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן. וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: For since Yosef the tzaddik informs him beforehand that afterward days of evil will come upon him, God forbid, and will seek to make him forget all that good, through this the discerning person will understand on his own that he must carefully store away all the good of the aspect of the seven years of plenty. That is, he should bind the holy desire in his thought and take this very matter into his awareness: even when his heart becomes stopped up through the awakening of evil in the destroyers, nevertheless he should strengthen himself in the service of Hashem by reminding himself of the first yearning, as above. And all the impressions of the first yearnings that he stored in the inwardness of his mind will be for him a deposit to revive his soul in days of evil, which are the aspect of the seven years of famine; in the aspect of “And the food shall be for a deposit for the land for the seven years of famine that will come afterward, and the land shall not be cut off through famine,” as above.

And all the impressions of the first yearnings that he stored in the inwardness of his mind will be for him a deposit to revive his soul in days of evil, which are the aspect of the seven years of famine; in the aspect of “And the food shall be for a deposit for the land for the seven years of famine that will come afterward, and the land shall not be cut off through famine,” as above.

segments.he:
קיום ישראל בגלות היה בזכות יוסף

"וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּר"

(מ״א, מט)

עִקַּר הַבֵּרוּר הוּא בִּבְחִינַת בֵּרוּר הָאֲכִילָה וְהַשְּׂבִיעָה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע מִשֶּׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. וְעַל כֵּן נָתַן עֵצָה וַיִּצְבְּרוּ בָר וְכוּ׳ וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן.

וְאִיתָא שֶׁבָּ״ר מְרַמֵּז עַל ר״ב נִיצוֹצוֹת מֵהָרפ״ח נִיצוֹצוֹת. שֶׁבֵּרֵר יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּ״ר וְכוּ׳, כַּמּוּבָא קלו.

הַיְנוּ שֶׁיּוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק נוֹתֵן עֵצָה לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לָחוּס עַל נַפְשׁוֹ, שֶׁיִּקְבֹּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר אֵיזֶה טוֹב בָּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, אֲזַי יִזְדָּרֵז תֵּכֶף לִצְבֹּר וְלֶאֱסֹף אֹכֶל הַשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּמָּהֵר לַחֲטֹף תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כָּל מַה שֶׁיּוּכַל בְּעֵת הַטּוֹבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כֹּל אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא יָדְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ עֲשֵׂה וְכוּ׳, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְמֵי רַע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לַעֲבֹר עַל הָאָדָם, שֶׁאָז יוּכַל לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַטּוֹב שֶׁקִּבֵּץ בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּימֵי נְעוּרָיו קלז. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה עִקַּר קִיּוּם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹקִים לִפְנֵיכֶם לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְכוּ׳. כִּי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְכֵן כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת בִּפְרָט גָּלוּת הָאַחֲרוֹן הַמַּר הַזֶּה שֶׁכֻּלָּם מְכֻנִּים בְּשֵׁם גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, כַּמּוּבָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ, בְּכֻלָּם לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לָנוּ לְהִתְקַיֵּם לוּלֵא ה׳ עֶזְרָתָה לָנוּ שֶׁהִקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְפָנֵינוּ צַדִּיקִים נוֹרָאִים כָּאֵלֶּה שֶׁעָמְדוּ בְּנִסְיוֹנוֹת רַבִּים אֵין מִסְפָּר שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהֵם מַמְשִׁיכִים עָלֵינוּ הֶאָרוֹת מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּכַמָּה וְכַמָּה דְּרָכִים נִפְלָאִים לְהַחֲיוֹתֵנוּ כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בִּבְחִינַת לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְלִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לִפְלֵיטָה גְּדֹלָה, אָמֵן וְאָמֵן קלח.

(הלכות בציעת הפת הלכה ה אות מ׳)
segments.en:
Israel’s continued existence in exile was through Joseph’s merit.

“And Joseph amassed grain.”

(41:49)

The principal refinement is in the aspect of refining eating and satiation, which is the aspect of refining the seven years of plenty from the seven years of famine. Therefore he gave the counsel, “And let them amass grain,” etc., “And the food shall be held in reserve.”

And it is stated that the printed expression ב״ר alludes to 202 sparks from the 288 sparks—the 202 sparks which Joseph refined in Egypt—as it is written, “And Joseph amassed בָּ״ר,” etc., as brought there [printed note marker קלו].

That is, Joseph the righteous gives counsel to everyone who wishes to have compassion upon his soul: he should gather all the food of the seven good years, etc. That is, when some good awakens within a person—which is the aspect of the seven years of plenty—he should immediately hasten to amass and gather the food of the good years, so that it will be held by him in reserve for the days of famine. That is, he should hasten to seize Torah, prayer, and good deeds, as much as he can during the good time, as it is written, “Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength,” etc., so that it will be held for him in reserve for the days of famine, Heaven forbid. These are the aspect of the evil days that a person must pass through, when he will be able to sustain himself with the good that he gathered at first in his youthful days [printed note marker קלז]. Therefore Israel’s principal continued existence in the Egyptian exile was through Joseph the righteous, as it is written, “For sustenance God sent me before you, to establish for you a remnant in the land,” etc. For the Egyptian exile, and likewise all the exiles—particularly this bitter final exile, all of which are called by the name of the Egyptian exile, as brought in the Midrash—in all of them it would have been impossible for us to endure had the Lord not come to our aid. He preceded the blow with its remedy by sending before us such awe-inspiring righteous men, who withstood innumerable trials, who are in the aspect of Joseph the righteous. They draw upon us illuminations from the root of our souls in the Torah, by many, many wondrous ways, to sustain us as on this day, in the aspect of “To establish for you a remnant in the land, and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.” Amen and amen [printed note marker קלח].

(Halachos of Bitseyas HaPas [Breaking Bread], Halacha 5, item 40)

pairs.he: עִקַּר הַבֵּרוּר הוּא בִּבְחִינַת בֵּרוּר הָאֲכִילָה וְהַשְּׂבִיעָה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע מִשֶּׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. וְעַל כֵּן נָתַן עֵצָה וַיִּצְבְּרוּ בָר וְכוּ׳ וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן.
pairs.en: The principal refinement is in the aspect of refining eating and satiation, which is the aspect of refining the seven years of plenty from the seven years of famine. Therefore he gave the counsel, “And let them amass grain,” etc., “And the food shall be held in reserve.”

pairs.he: וְאִיתָא שֶׁבָּ״ר מְרַמֵּז עַל ר״ב נִיצוֹצוֹת מֵהָרפ״ח נִיצוֹצוֹת. שֶׁבֵּרֵר יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּ״ר וְכוּ׳, כַּמּוּבָא קלו.
pairs.en: And it is stated that the printed expression ב״ר alludes to 202 sparks from the 288 sparks—the 202 sparks which Joseph refined in Egypt—as it is written, “And Joseph amassed בָּ״ר,” etc., as brought there [printed note marker קלו].

pairs.he: הַיְנוּ שֶׁיּוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק נוֹתֵן עֵצָה לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לָחוּס עַל נַפְשׁוֹ, שֶׁיִּקְבֹּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר אֵיזֶה טוֹב בָּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, אֲזַי יִזְדָּרֵז תֵּכֶף לִצְבֹּר וְלֶאֱסֹף אֹכֶל הַשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּמָּהֵר לַחֲטֹף תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כָּל מַה שֶׁיּוּכַל בְּעֵת הַטּוֹבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כֹּל אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא יָדְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ עֲשֵׂה וְכוּ׳, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְמֵי רַע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לַעֲבֹר עַל הָאָדָם, שֶׁאָז יוּכַל לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַטּוֹב שֶׁקִּבֵּץ בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּימֵי נְעוּרָיו קלז. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה עִקַּר קִיּוּם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹקִים לִפְנֵיכֶם לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְכוּ׳. כִּי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְכֵן כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת בִּפְרָט גָּלוּת הָאַחֲרוֹן הַמַּר הַזֶּה שֶׁכֻּלָּם מְכֻנִּים בְּשֵׁם גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, כַּמּוּבָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ, בְּכֻלָּם לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לָנוּ לְהִתְקַיֵּם לוּלֵא ה׳ עֶזְרָתָה לָנוּ שֶׁהִקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְפָנֵינוּ צַדִּיקִים נוֹרָאִים כָּאֵלֶּה שֶׁעָמְדוּ בְּנִסְיוֹנוֹת רַבִּים אֵין מִסְפָּר שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהֵם מַמְשִׁיכִים עָלֵינוּ הֶאָרוֹת מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּכַמָּה וְכַמָּה דְּרָכִים נִפְלָאִים לְהַחֲיוֹתֵנוּ כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בִּבְחִינַת לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְלִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לִפְלֵיטָה גְּדֹלָה, אָמֵן וְאָמֵן קלח.
pairs.en: That is, Joseph the righteous gives counsel to everyone who wishes to have compassion upon his soul: he should gather all the food of the seven good years, etc. That is, when some good awakens within a person—which is the aspect of the seven years of plenty—he should immediately hasten to amass and gather the food of the good years, so that it will be held by him in reserve for the days of famine. That is, he should hasten to seize Torah, prayer, and good deeds, as much as he can during the good time, as it is written, “Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength,” etc., so that it will be held for him in reserve for the days of famine, Heaven forbid. These are the aspect of the evil days that a person must pass through, when he will be able to sustain himself with the good that he gathered at first in his youthful days [printed note marker קלז]. Therefore Israel’s principal continued existence in the Egyptian exile was through Joseph the righteous, as it is written, “For sustenance God sent me before you, to establish for you a remnant in the land,” etc. For the Egyptian exile, and likewise all the exiles—particularly this bitter final exile, all of which are called by the name of the Egyptian exile, as brought in the Midrash—in all of them it would have been impossible for us to endure had the Lord not come to our aid. He preceded the blow with its remedy by sending before us such awe-inspiring righteous men, who withstood innumerable trials, who are in the aspect of Joseph the righteous. They draw upon us illuminations from the root of our souls in the Torah, by many, many wondrous ways, to sustain us as on this day, in the aspect of “To establish for you a remnant in the land, and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.” Amen and amen [printed note marker קלח].

בכנפי יונה (ח״ג סימן נ״ו) כתב כן. ואחריו הביאו זה מגדולי המקובלים ז״ל. ומהם, הרמ״ז ז״ל בביאורו לזוה״ק פרשת ויקהל כתב: לבתר סטא זינא לזיניה, פי׳ שצד הרע גבר בהם. ועוד י״ל כמ״ש בכתבי הרב, כי מאותם הרפ״ח ניצוצין נכללו ר״ב בחינות מהם והיו קרובים להתקן, ונשארו פ״ו השרשיות והחזקות, ואלמלא כוונה רעה של ערב רב בשעת מתן תורה היה מתקן הכל, אבל הם גנבו שור מן המרכבה דתמן שם אלקים אחור ליפול ר״ב, וז״ש סטא זינא לזיניה, הר״ב הלך לו אצל הפ״ו. ואתי אינון ערב רב ולכן נטמעו מן הקדושה. ע״כ. והרמה״ש ז״ל בהגהות האוצרות חיים (אות ס״ג) כתב: נקדים לך הקדמה א׳ מ״ש האר״י ז״ל בפמ״א וז״ל כי רפ״ח ניצוצות שנפלו שבירי כלים שנפלו לתה״ר וכו׳ וישראל כשהיו במצרים העלה משם ר״ב ניצוצות, אבל פ״ו ניצו׳ לתשלום רפ״ח לא היה יכול מרע״ה להוציא משם מכור הברזל. וז״ש וגם ערב ר״ב עלה אתם, ר״ב דייקא ולא יותר וכו׳. שכל זה נרמז במ״ש עה״פ יעקב לבניו שמעתי כי יש שבר במצרים, שבר דייקא דהיינו על הניצוצין דשברי כלים, דדע שעמדו על פ״ו, ר״ל לא ישאר שם רק פ״ו, וזהו ושברו ׳לנו׳ גימטריא פ״ו וכו׳. וזה אפשר מש״ה ושברו לנו וכו׳ ונחיה ולא נמות, כמ״ש בכוונות האר״י זללה״ה שאלו השברים הם סיבת מיתה לבני עולם, וכשיצאו אותם השברים אז בלע המות, וזהו ׳ונחיה ולא נמות׳. ע״כ ע״ש. בעל התניא בספרו תורה אור פרשת בא (עמ׳ 120) כתב: בעצם היום הזה יצאו צבאות הוי״ה, הוא לשון סמוך שהצבאות נטפל לשם הוי״ה, אבל אינו לשון שם התואר כמ״ש הוי״ה צבאות. והיינו, בחי׳ הניצוצות שנתבררו בגלות דמצרים נתעלו ליכלל בשם הוי״ה, הם הנק׳ צבאות הוי״ה. כי רפ״ח ניצוצות נפלו בשבירת הכלים ומה נתברר בגלות מצרים ר״ב ניצוצים, וע״ז נאמר וינצלו את מצרים. וז״ש וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, וכתיב רב לך וכו׳. ע״כ. בקהלת יעקב (ערך רפ) וז״ל: רפ״ח ניצוצין מז׳ מלכין דמיתו נפלו בשברי כלים, וזה סוד ורוח אלהים מרחפת רפ״ח מת, ובמצרים העלו ר״ב ניצוצין, זה שאמר וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, זה שאמר וירדו אחי יוסף לשבור ב״ר במצרים, ופ״ו נשאר לתקן עד ביאת משיחנו, וזה שאמר ורוח אלהים וזה רוח זה רוחו של משיח נשאר לו לתקן פ״ו ניצוצין כמנין אלהים. (מפרוש תלמיד הרב על ספרא דצניעותא דף קכ״ו ע״ב). ע״כ. הפלא יועץ ז״ל בספרו עץ השדה ׳אלף המגן׳ (מפתח תולדות, מתן לך) מזכיר זאת: ויתן לך האלקים מטל השמים טל תורה מן השמים ועל ידה תוציא משמני הארץ שהם ניצוה״ק הטמונים בארץ ולא תצטרך לגלות מצרים כדי להוציא ר״ב ניצוצות כמ״ש המקובלים על פסוק וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, אלא ׳ורב׳ על ידך דגן ותירוש שהוא תשב״כ ותשבע״פ. ע״כ. ועוד טובא בספרי הצדיקים ז״ל. (עי׳ ספר ׳תכלית חכמה׳ בזה)

In Kanfay Yonah (part 3, section 56) he wrote thus. After him, great kabbalists of blessed memory brought this. Among them, RMZ, of blessed memory, in his explanation of the holy Zohar, the portion Vayakhel, wrote: “Afterward, a kind inclined toward its kind”—that is, the evil side prevailed within them. It may further be said, as is written in the master’s writings, that of those 288 sparks, 202 aspects of them were included and were close to being repaired, while the 86 root and strong ones remained. Were it not for the evil intention of the mixed multitude at the giving of the Torah, he would have repaired everything. But they stole the ox from the chariot, where there is the name Elokim, “backward to fall 202” [opaque phrase]; this is “a kind inclined toward its kind”: the 202 went over to the 86. “And those of the mixed multitude came,” and therefore they were submerged away from holiness. End of quotation. RMHSh, of blessed memory, in the glosses to Oatzroas Chaim (item 63), wrote: Let us preface for you one introduction, what the Ari of blessed memory wrote in PMA, in these words: For the 288 sparks that fell—broken vessels that fell to THR, etc.—and Israel, when they were in Egypt, raised 202 sparks from there. But 86 sparks, to complete the 288, Moshe Rabbainu, peace be upon him, was not able to bring out from there, from the iron furnace. This is “And also a mixed multitude—202—went up with them”: precisely 202, and no more, etc. All this is hinted at in what is written on the verse, “Yaakov, to his sons: I heard that there is grain in Egypt” [printed incipit retained]: precisely “brokenness,” meaning the sparks of the broken vessels; know that they stood at 86—that is, only 86 would remain there. This is “And buy for us”: “for us” has the numerical value 86, etc. This may be what Scripture says, “And buy for us,” etc., “and we shall live and not die,” as is written in the Ari’s intentions, may his memory be for the life of the World to Come, that these fragments cause death for the people of the world; when those fragments go out, then “He has swallowed up death.” This is “and we shall live and not die.” End of quotation; see there. The author of Tanya, in his book Torah Oar, the portion Bo (p. 120), wrote: “On this very day the hosts of the Divine Name went out” is a construct expression: the hosts are subordinate to the Divine Name; it is not an expression of a descriptive name, as in “the Divine Name of Hosts.” That is, the sparks refined in the Egyptian exile were elevated to be included in the Divine Name; they are called “the hosts of the Divine Name.” For 288 sparks fell in the breaking of the vessels, and what was refined in the Egyptian exile was 202 sparks. Concerning this it was said, “And they emptied Egypt.” This is “And also a mixed multitude went up with them,” and it is written, “It is much for you,” etc. End of quotation. In Kihilas Yaakov (entry רפ), in these words: The 288 sparks from the seven kings who died fell in the fragments of vessels. This is the secret of “And the spirit of God was hovering”: 288, dead. In Egypt they raised 202 sparks. This is what it says, “And also a mixed multitude went up with them”; this is what it says, “And Yosef’s brothers descended to buy grain”—BR—in Egypt. And 86 remained to be repaired until the coming of our Messiah. This is what it says, “And the spirit of God”: this spirit is the spirit of the Messiah; it remains for him to repair 86 sparks, the numerical value of Elokim. (From the explanation of the master’s disciple on Sifra DiTzneeoosuh, folio 126, side b.) End of quotation. The Pele Yoetz, of blessed memory, in his book Aitz HaSudeh, “Elef HaMugen” (index of Toaldoas, “grant you”), mentions this: “And God shall grant you of the dew of heaven”—the dew of Torah from heaven; through it you shall bring out of the fatness of the earth, which are the holy sparks hidden in the earth, and you will not have to go into Egyptian exile to bring out 202 sparks, as the kabbalists wrote on the verse “And also a mixed multitude went up with them,” but “abundant” grain and wine through you, which is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. End of quotation. There is much more in the books of the righteous, of blessed memory. (See the book Tachlis Chokhmah concerning this.)
