This is the aspect of his occupying himself with urging that all novel Torah insights be written in books, multiplying books without end, which is the principal preservation of the foods of Torah. For the book is for remembrance, the aspect of “Write this as a remembrance in the book,” so that it will be preserved forever and will not be lost and forgotten.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּר כְּחוֹל הַיָּם עַד כִּי חָדַל לִסְפֹּר כִּי אֵין מִסְפָּר, בְּחִינַת עֲשׂוֹת סְפָרִים הַרְבֵּה אֵין קֵץ כִּי בְּיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ, וְזָקֵן זֶה קָנָה חָכְמָה קָנָה בִּינָה. שֶׁמְּרֻמָּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין בּוֹ הַסְּפָרִים שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה תִּהְיֶה עִקַּר הַגְּאֻלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בר״מ וּבְגָלוּתָא קַדְמָאָה בְּמַטֶּה דִּילָךְ בְּזַע יָמָא, וּבְגָלוּתָא בַּתְרָאָה בְּקָנֶה דִילָךְ דְּאִיהוּ קֻלְמָסָא בְּזַע יַמָּא דְאוֹרַיְתָא.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of “And Yosef amassed grain like the sand of the sea until he ceased counting, for there was no number,” the aspect of “making many books has no end.” For concerning Yosef it is said, “For he was a son of old age to him,” and “an elder”—one who has acquired wisdom, acquired understanding—which alludes to the reed and pen with which the books of the holy Torah are written, through which the principal redemption will come about. As stated in the holy Zohar, in Raaya Mehemna: “And in the first exile, with your staff split the sea, and in the final exile, with your reed, which is a pen, split the sea of Torah.”

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה כִּי הַמְּנוֹרָה הַטְּהוֹרָה זֶה בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעִקַּר קִיּוּמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַקָּנִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּסִים הַכּוֹתְבִים סִפְרֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעַל יָדָם עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁהוּא תִּקּוּן הָעֵצָה.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, for the pure Menorah is the aspect of the light of Torah, whose principal endurance is through the reeds, which are the aspect of the pens with which books of novel Torah insights are written; through them comes the principal rectification, which is the rectification of counsel.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, for the pure Menorah is the aspect of the light of Torah, whose principal endurance is through the reeds, which are the aspect of the pens with which books of novel Torah insights are written; through them comes the principal rectification, which is the rectification of counsel.

pairs.he: וְיֵשׁ לְרַמֵּז שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ. בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעָה קָנִים בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעַת קְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּחִינַת כְּלַל הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנִים שֶׁכְּלוּלִים בְּשִׁבְעָה בְּחִינַת חָצְבָה עַמּוּדֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה, לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם כָּל חֲלֻקַּת הָעֵצָה לְבָרֵר הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים הַטּוֹבוֹת לְבָרְרָם מֵהַהֵפֶךְ הָרוֹצִים לְבַלְּעָם כַּנַּ״ל. וְעַל כֵּן מְרַמֵּז הַשֶּׁבַע הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הַתִּקּוּן אֵיךְ לְבָרְרָם שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שִׁבֳּלִים עֹלוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד בְּרִיאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת בְּקָנֶה אֶחָד מְרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה הַנַּ״ל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַקֻּלְמוּס הַכּוֹתֶבֶת סִפְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּ׳ וְכַנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And one may hint that this is the aspect of “for he was a son of old age to him”: the aspect of seven reeds, the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, the aspect of the totality of the holy books written with reeds, which are encompassed in seven, the aspect of “she has hewn her seven pillars,” to rectify all seven attributes in which all the divisions of counsel lie, to refine the seven good attributes, which are the seven good cows and the seven good ears of grain—to refine them from their opposite, which seeks to swallow them, as above. Therefore the seven ears of grain hint at the rectification, how to refine them: this is the aspect of “seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, healthy and good.” “On one stalk” alludes to the aforesaid reed, which is the aspect of the pen writing the books of Torah, etc., as above, through which the principal rectification comes, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And one may hint that this is the aspect of “for he was a son of old age to him”: the aspect of seven reeds, the aspect of the seven branches of the Menorah, the aspect of the totality of the holy books written with reeds, which are encompassed in seven, the aspect of “she has hewn her seven pillars,” to rectify all seven attributes in which all the divisions of counsel lie, to refine the seven good attributes, which are the seven good cows and the seven good ears of grain—to refine them from their opposite, which seeks to swallow them, as above. Therefore the seven ears of grain hint at the rectification, how to refine them: this is the aspect of “seven ears of grain coming up on one stalk, healthy and good.” “On one stalk” alludes to the aforesaid reed, which is the aspect of the pen writing the books of Torah, etc., as above, through which the principal rectification comes, as above.

pairs.he: וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר, וּמוּבָא בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל הַקָּנֶה וְהַקֻּלְמוּס שֶׁהוּא חָבֵר לְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁיִּתְחַכְּמוּ דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה. וְזֶה עֲשֵׂה לְךָ רַב וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי וּקְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר הַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי הַסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַנִּכְתָּבִים בְּקָנֶה תְּחַבֵּר אוֹתָם אֵלֶיךָ וּתְעַיֵּן בָּהֶם הֵיטֵב וְתוּכַל לֵידַע מִי הוּא הָרַב הָאֱמֶת. כִּי עִקַּר הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַסְּפָרִים כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself and acquire a friend for yourself,” and it is cited in books that this alludes to the reed and pen, which is a friend to the Torah scholar, so that words of Torah become wiser through this. And this is “Make a Rabbi for yourself”; and if he cannot find the rectification, [it is] through “and acquire a friend for yourself”: namely, through the holy books written with a reed—join them to yourself and study them carefully, and you will be able to know who is the true Rabbi. For the principal rectification is through multiplying books, as above.

This is a qualified integrated-English reading, not a claim that the printed first full stop is an English sentence boundary. The repeated return/gain-strength argument is not deduplicated. Both animal [level] and vegetable [level] glosses remain inherited editorial glosses; higher attaches to the animal-level refining, good cows to that level, full/good ears to vegetable refining. But against this too is an independent contrast with sitra achra and confusions as subjects, and until introduces the swallowing by the empty/evil ears. Preserve plural them without assigning a new doctrinal referent. No new consequent, then, actor or copula is supplied.

This passage only: The complete native report has the impersonal citation formula כמו שאיתא and literal בר״מ, plus two clauses with your staff/your reed as instrumental phrases and the same bare consonantal operative verb בזע before sea/sea of Torah. Scoped native frame inspection confirms no printed named actor, ת suffix or passive prefix in either occurrence; this is not vowel certification. Current bare English split after an initial with phrase invites a command reading. Bare בזע without an expressed subject does not securely choose an unexpressed active declarative agent versus an addressed imperative from these local clauses; first/final exile contrasts do not license supplying a named actor or tense. Passive was/will be split suppresses that voice distinction; nominal splitting suppresses finite force; intransitive the sea split changes the operative active relation. None preserves all actual alternatives as a complete English after. Null complete-field hold, not a repaired citation. The preceding Yosef grain/no-count, books/no-end, old age, elder/acquired wisdom/acquired understanding, reed/pen and principal-redemption relations are read and conserved as context, not accepted separately. The current qualified Raaya Mehemna rendering remains a qualified rendering of בר״מ, not newly expanded attribution. No external quotation, actor, object or source vowels added. This passage only: Later Therefore at ועל כן continues the prior seven-reeds/books/attributes inference; another And is not obligatory. It is distinct from opening And-one-may-hint. Seven reeds/branches, books/inclusion and seven pillars do not count books or pens. Good attributes/cows/ears are refined from their opposite; singular “opposite” retains a collective head with plural desiring forces. Later ears hint at remedy; quoted one stalk differs from its repeated gloss and refers to the later singular pen, not earlier plural pens. Both references and principal rectification remain.

Reed/pen as friend of the Torah scholar and the purpose that words of Torah become wiser are conserved. The current comma and [it is] commit to the latter attachment without resolving the omitted object or predicate. The shift to imperatives join/study and you will know the true Rabbi and the final multiplying-books rationale are all read, but do not make the prior attachment unique. pairs.he: ״וְהִנֵּה מִן הַיְאֹר עֹלֹת שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת יְפוֹת מַרְאֶה וּבְרִיאֹת בָּשָׂר״ וְגוֹ׳ (מ״א, ב) עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ הַמְּדַבֵּר מִשְּׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן בְּלִקּוּטֵי הָרִאשׁוֹן סִימָן נד, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵרֹאשׁוֹ לְסוֹפוֹ.
pairs.en: “And behold, from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and healthy in flesh,” etc. (41:2), according to the teaching “And it was at the end,” which discusses preserving memory, in Likutay, the first [collection], section 54; see there the entire teaching from its beginning to its end.

pairs.he: וְהַכְּלָל כִּי צְרִיכִין לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד אֶת הַזִּכָּרוֹן, הַיְנוּ לְאַדְבְּקָא מַחֲשַׁבְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי לִזְכֹּר תָּמִיד בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ אֶת עוֹלָם הַנִּצְחִי שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְלֹא יִפֹּל לְשִׁכְחָה שֶׁהוּא מִיתַת הַלֵּב, שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח אֶת עוֹלָם הַבָּא כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו וּשְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן הוּא בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם מַה שֶּׁמְּבֹאָר עַל פָּסוּק ה׳ אֱלֹקַי גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד וְכוּ׳. וְאֵצֶל הֲמוֹן עַם נַעֲשֶׂה כָּל זֶה מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי שֵׁנָה וְצִיצִית וּתְפִלִּין וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּתְפִלָּה וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
pairs.en: And the principle is that one must guard memory very carefully: namely, to attach thought to the world to come, constantly remembering in his thought the eternal world, which is the world to come, and not fall into forgetfulness, which is the death of the heart, so that he not forget the world to come throughout all the days of his life. Preserving memory is in general and in particular, etc.; see there what is explained concerning the verse “Hashem my God, You are very great,” etc. And among the general populace all this comes about of itself through sleep and tzitzis and tefillin, the recitation of Shema, prayer and commerce; see there.

qualifiedAfter.en: And the principle is that one must guard memory very carefully: namely, to attach thought to the world to come, constantly remembering in his thought the eternal world, which is the world to come, and not fall into forgetfulness, which is the death of the heart, so that he not forget the world to come throughout all the days of his life. Preserving memory is in general and in particular, etc.; see there what is explained concerning the verse “Hashem my God, You are very great,” etc. And among the general populace all this comes about of itself through sleep and tzitzis and tefillin, the recitation of Shema, prayer and commerce; see there.

pairs.he: וּמְבֹאָר שָׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כָּל הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד צַדִּיק וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נוֹטֶה שָׁמַיִם כַּיְרִיעָה, כִּי בְּכָל הַדְּבָרִים יֵשׁ נִיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים וְעַל יְדֵי הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן נִתְחַבְּרִין וְנִתְעַלִּין הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת כְּפִי חֶלְקֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד צַדִּיק וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַיֵּן שָׁם הֵיטֵב. וְלִשְׁמֹר הַזִּכָּרוֹן צְרִיכִין לִשְׁמֹר עַצְמוֹ מֵרַע עַיִן וְכוּ׳ גַּם צְרִיכִים לִשְׁמֹר עַצְמוֹ מִכֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פַּרְעֹה וְכוּ׳ וְכוּ׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם כָּל זֶה הֵיטֵב.
pairs.en: And it is explained there that through all commerce a unification of the tzaddik and the Congregation of Israel is made, which is the aspect of “stretching the heavens like a curtain.” For in all things there are holy sparks, and through commerce the sparks become joined and elevated according to the portions of nefesh, ru’ach and neshamah that each person has; through this a unification of the tzaddik and the Congregation of Israel is made; see there carefully. To preserve memory one must guard oneself from an evil eye, etc.; one must also guard oneself from the imaginative faculty, which is the aspect of Pharaoh, etc., etc.; see all this there carefully.

pairs.he: וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, בְּחִינַת עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְעֹה בְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי פַּרְעֹה הוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה, בְּחִינַת פְּגַם הַזִּכָּרוֹן בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, כַּמְבֹאָר שָׁם, וְעַל כֵּן רָצָה לְהַגְבִּיר בְּחִינַת הָעַבְדוּת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּדֵי לְהַפִּיל עֲלֵיהֶם שִׁכְחָה כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לְאַדְבֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי נִרְפִּים הֵם עַל כֵּן הֵם צוֹעֲקִים לֵאמֹר נֵלְכָה וְנִזְבְּחָה לֵאלֹקֵינוּ תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבוֹדָה וְיַעֲשׂוּ בָהּ וְאַל יִשְׁעוּ וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of the exile in Egypt, the aspect of “We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt,” for Pharaoh is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of the blemish in memory, the aspect of forgetfulness, as explained there. Therefore he wanted to strengthen the aspect of servitude over Israel, to cast forgetfulness upon them so that they could not attach their thought to the world to come, as it is written, “For they are idle; therefore they cry out, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God. Let the work be heavy, and let them labor in it, and let them not turn,” etc.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of the exile in Egypt, the aspect of “We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt,” for Pharaoh is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of the blemish in memory, the aspect of forgetfulness, as explained there. Let the work be heavy, and let them labor in it, and let them not turn,” etc.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁהִבְטִיחַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּגָלוּת בִּבְחִינַת עַבְדוּת אֵצֶל פַּרְעֹה שֶׁכָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, כִּי זֶה הָעֲשִׁירוּת הַגָּדוֹל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁזָּכוּ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר נִיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מִן הַקְּלִפּוֹת קלד שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַזִּכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְתַּקֵּן פְּגַם הָעַבְדוּת וְהַגָּלוּת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of what Hashem, blessed be He, promised Avraham our forefather: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” That is, He promised him that although they would be in exile in the aspect of servitude with Pharaoh, all of which is the aspect of forgetfulness, afterward they would go out with great possessions. For this great wealth of holiness that they merited in the Exodus from Egypt is the aspect of refining holy sparks from the klipos [printed note marker: 134], which is the aspect of rectifying memory. Therefore through this the blemish of servitude and exile, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, was rectified, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is the aspect of what Hashem, blessed be He, promised Avraham our forefather: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” That is, He promised him that although they would be in exile in the aspect of servitude with Pharaoh, all of which is the aspect of forgetfulness, afterward they would go out with great possessions. For this great wealth of holiness that they merited in the Exodus from Egypt is the aspect of refining holy sparks from the klipos [printed note marker: 134], which is the aspect of rectifying memory. Therefore through this the blemish of servitude and exile, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, was rectified, as above.

pairs.he: וּפָרָה הוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, כִּי עִקַּר הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא מִבְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל, וְעִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא בִּבְחִינַת פָּרָה בְּיוֹתֵר, כִּי הִיא עִקַּר הַבַּהֲמִיּוּת כִּי מֶלֶךְ שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שׁוֹר (חגיגה דף י״ג ע״ב) וְכָל הַבְּהֵמוֹת כְּלוּלִים בּוֹ וְעִקַּר אֲחִיזַת הַשִּׁכְחָה בִּבְחִינַת בַּהֲמִיּוּת כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And a cow is the aspect of forgetfulness, for forgetfulness principally comes from the aspect of the imaginative faculty, which is the power of animality, as explained in the aforesaid teaching. The chief animality and forgetfulness are particularly in the aspect of a cow, for she is the principal animality, for “the king among the animals is the ox” (Chagigah, folio 13b)—and all the animals are encompassed in it, and forgetfulness principally takes hold in the aspect of animality, as above.

qualifiedAfter.en: And a cow is the aspect of forgetfulness, for forgetfulness principally comes from the aspect of the imaginative faculty, which is the power of animality, as explained in the aforesaid teaching. The chief animality and forgetfulness are particularly in the aspect of a cow, for she is the principal animality, for “the king among the animals is the ox” (Chagigah, folio 13b)—and all the animals are encompassed in it, and forgetfulness principally takes hold in the aspect of animality, as above.

pairs.he: וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ, כִּי דְּכוּרָא נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם זָכוֹר, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמִּשָּׁם בְּחִינַת זִכָּרוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בַּבְּהֵמוֹת נֶאֱחָז הַשִּׁכְחָה בְּיוֹתֵר בִּבְחִינַת הַנּוּקְבָא שֶׁל הַשּׁוֹר שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ וְהַכְּלָל שֶׁבַּבְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁהִיא הַפָּרָה. וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא הַשַּׂר שֶׁל שִׁכְחָה פּוּרָה, עַל שֵׁם פָּרָה כּמובא קלה.
pairs.en: And forgetfulness is from the feminine side, as is known, for the masculine is named after “remember,” because from there is the aspect of memory. Therefore even among the animals forgetfulness takes hold particularly in the aspect of the female of the ox, which is the head and totality among the animals, namely the cow. Therefore the minister of forgetfulness is called Purah, after parah, a cow, as cited [printed note marker: 135].

qualifiedAfter.en: And forgetfulness is from the feminine side, as is known, for the masculine is named after “remember,” because from there is the aspect of memory. Therefore the minister of forgetfulness is called Purah, after parah, a cow, as cited [printed note marker: 135].

pairs.he: וְזֶה כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִים אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְסָרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ כְּתִיב כִּי כְּפָרָה סוֹרֵרָה סָרַר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
pairs.en: And this is that when Israel are reproved for having forgotten Hashem, blessed be He, and turned away from Him, it is written, “For like a rebellious cow, Israel rebelled.”

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is that when Israel are reproved for having forgotten Hashem, blessed be He, and turned away from Him, it is written, “For like a rebellious cow, Israel rebelled.”

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה כֹּחַ הַבַּטֵּל כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה הַנַּ״ל וְרָצָה לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַמְשִׁיכָם לְגָלוּת וְעַבְדוּת תַּחַת יָדוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה, לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶת הַזִּכָּרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִים לְדַבֵּק מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם שָׁם, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁהֵם הִתְחִילוּ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ זֶה הַזִּכָּרוֹן בָּעוֹלָם כִּי הֵם הוֹדִיעוּ וְגִלּוּ אֱלֹקוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם (וכמבואר מזה במקום אחר).
pairs.en: And therefore Pharaoh, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the idle faculty, as explained in the aforesaid teaching, wanted to prevail over Israel and draw them into exile and servitude under his hand, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, to make them forget, God forbid, the remembrance of the world to come, to which they were accustomed to attach their thought, according to what they received from their forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who began to draw this remembrance into the world, for they made known and revealed His divinity in the world (as explained concerning this elsewhere).

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore Pharaoh, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the idle faculty, as explained in the aforesaid teaching, wanted to prevail over Israel and draw them into exile and servitude under his hand, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, to make them forget, God forbid, the remembrance of the world to come, to which they were accustomed to attach their thought, according to what they received from their forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who began to draw this remembrance into the world, for they made known and revealed His divinity in the world (as explained concerning this elsewhere).

pairs.he: עַל כֵּן רָאָה פַּרְעֹה בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא, שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְשֶׁבַע פָּרוֹת רָעוֹת וְשֶׁאָכְלוּ הַפָּרוֹת הָרָעוֹת אֶת הַטּוֹבוֹת וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה, שֶׁכָּל זֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁיִּתְגַּבֵּר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָרַע עַל הַטּוֹב עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁכַּח הַטּוֹב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת וְנִשְׁכַּח כָּל הַשָּׂבָע וְכוּ׳. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה חֲלוֹמוֹ פָּרוֹת דַּיְקָא כִּי שָׁם עִקַּר אֲחִיזַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פָּרָה כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: Therefore Pharaoh saw cows specifically in his dream: seven good cows and seven evil cows, and the evil cows ate the good ones, “and it was not known that they had entered into their inward parts.” All this indicates that evil would prevail over good, God forbid, until good is forgotten, God forbid, in the aspect of “and all the plenty shall be forgotten,” etc. Therefore his dream was specifically cows, for there Pharaoh principally takes hold, who is the aspect of the imaginative faculty, the aspect of forgetfulness, which is the aspect of a cow, as above.

pairs.he: אֲבָל הַתִּקּוּן הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף, כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁפָּתַר יוֹסֵף אֶת הַחֲלוֹם לְפַרְעֹה וְנַעֲשָׂה מֶלֶךְ וְקִבֵּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁבַר וּבִטֵּל אֶת הָרָעָב וְהִגְבִּיר הַטּוֹב עַל הָרַע, וְעַל יְדֵי קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ הִכְנִיעַ הַזֻּהֲמָא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָצֵאת מִשָּׁם. כִּי עִקַּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בְּכֹחַ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
pairs.en: But the rectification was through Yosef, for through Yosef interpreting the dream for Pharaoh and becoming king and gathering all the food of the seven good years, through this he broke and annulled the famine and strengthened good over evil; and through his holiness he subdued the pollution of Egypt, and through this Israel merited to leave there. For the Exodus from Egypt was principally through the power of Yosef the tzaddik, as it is written, “And Moshe took Yosef’s bones with him,” as stated in the holy Zohar.

qualifiedAfter.en: But the rectification was through Yosef, for through Yosef interpreting the dream for Pharaoh and becoming king and gathering all the food of the seven good years, through this he broke and annulled the famine and strengthened good over evil; and through his holiness he subdued the pollution of Egypt, and through this Israel merited to leave there. For the Exodus from Egypt was principally through the power of Yosef the tzaddik, as it is written, “And Moshe took Yosef’s bones with him,” as stated in the holy Zohar.

pairs.he: כִּי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן, הוּא מַכְנִיעַ בְּחִינַת פַּרְעֹה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שִׁכְחָה וּמְבָרֵר הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִן הַשִּׁכְחָה, וְעַל כֵּן הוּא יוֹדֵעַ לִפְתֹּר הַחֲלוֹם שֶׁל הַפָּרוֹת וּלְהַכְנִיעַ וּלְבַטֵּל הַשִּׁכְחָה הַנֶּאֱחָז בָּהֶם שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב, כִּי הוּא מַגְבִּיר הַשָּׂבָע עַל הָרָעָב וּמַמְשִׁיךְ כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת וְהַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: For Yosef, who is the aspect of preserving memory, subdues the aspect of Pharaoh, which is the aspect of forgetfulness, and refines memory out of forgetfulness. Therefore he knows how to interpret the dream of the cows and subdue and annul the forgetfulness that takes hold in them, which is the seven years of famine, for he strengthens plenty over famine and draws all beneficence and blessings through preserving memory, from which all blessings proceed, as above.

pairs.he: מפורסם זה בספה״ק, כגון הבאר מים חיים (בתחילת פרשת וישב): שיעקב ובניו ירדו מצרימה הכל היה לפי שהם תולדות יעקב והוא קיבל עליו ועל זרעו אחריו להיות גרים בארץ לא להם ועבדום וענו אותם בכדי לצאת ברכוש גדול, להוציא כל ניצוצות של הקדושה שהיו מוטבעים במעמקי קליפת מצרים לקחת בלעם מפיהם להיות חיל בלע ויקיאנו. ע״כ. וכן בזרע קודש בפרשת בא (דבר נא וגו׳) וז״ל: כדי שלא יאמר אותו צדיק וכו׳ ואחרי כן יצאו ברכוש גדול לא קיים בהם. על זה יש לתמוה וכי חשוד אותו צדיק אברהם ע״ה שיתרעם וכו׳, ועוד, וכי היה אברהם מבקש רכוש של ממון אדרבא היה שונא רכוש כמו שמצינו במלחמת ד׳ מלכים וכו׳. והנה גלות מצרים היה עיקר הכונה שיוציאו ישראל משם כל ניצוצות הקדושות שנפלו בקליפה כמבואר כמה פעמים בזוה״ק שזה הוא עיקר הרכוש הפנימי אשר הוציאו ישראל ממצרים. ע״כ. ועוד טובא.
pairs.en: This is well known in the holy books, for example B’ear Mayim Chayim (at the beginning of the parsha Vayeishev): That Yaakov and his sons went down to Egypt—all of it was because they were the descendants of Yaakov, and he accepted upon himself and upon his seed after him that they should be strangers in a land not theirs, “and they will enslave them and afflict them,” in order to go out with great wealth: to bring out all the sparks of holiness that were embedded in the depths of the klipah of Egypt, to take what they had swallowed out of their mouths, so that “He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out.” Thus far. And likewise in Zera Kodesh in the parsha Bo (“Speak, please,” etc.), and these are its words: So that that righteous man should not say, etc., “and afterward they will go out with great wealth” He did not fulfill for them. Concerning this one must wonder: Is that righteous man Avraham, peace be upon him, suspected of complaining, etc.? And furthermore, was Avraham seeking monetary wealth? On the contrary, he hated wealth, as we find in the war of the four kings, etc. And behold, the principal intention of the Egyptian exile was that Israel should bring out from there all the holy sparks that had fallen into the klipah, as is explained many times in the holy Zohar, that this is the principal inward wealth that Israel brought out of Egypt. Thus far. And much more besides.

pairs.he: ״וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן״ וְגוֹ׳ ״וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב״ (מ״א, לו) זֶה בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁל חֲלוֹם פַּרְעֹה, שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עֵצָה שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם הַשִּׂבְעָה וְהַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמֹּחִין שֶׁל חוּץ לָאָרֶץ.
pairs.en: “And the food shall be for a deposit,” etc., “and the land shall not be cut off through famine” (41:36). This is the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of the rectification of Pharaoh’s dream, who gives counsel so that the satiation and good of the seven years of plenty will endure, and the land will not be cut off through famine, which is the aspect of the mental faculties of outside the Land.

pairs.he: וַעֲצָתוֹ הוּא שֶׁיִּקְבְּצוּ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטֹּבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר עַל הָאָדָם אֵיזֶה טוֹב בְּחִינַת קְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמִּשָּׁם כָּל הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת, אָז תֵּכֶף יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה עֻבְדָּא דִקְדֻשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתוֹ, לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אוֹ לִלְמֹד אוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה, וְיַעֲשֶׂה לְעַצְמוֹ אוֹצָרוֹת בְּמֹחוֹ לְהַטְמִין שָׁם אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת, כִּי הָאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּחִירָה וְיֵשׁ כֹּחַ בְּיָדוֹ כְּשֶׁבָּא עָלָיו אֵיזֶה תְּשׁוּקָה טוֹבָה, לְהַטְמִין וּלְקַשֵּׁר אוֹתָהּ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ וְלִקַּח בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ זֹאת הַתְּשׁוּקָה לְזָכְרָהּ הֵיטֵב שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכָּחֶנָּה.
pairs.en: And his counsel is that they gather all the food of these seven good years, “and the food shall be for a deposit,” etc. That is, immediately when some good awakens upon a person, the aspect of the holiness of the Land of Israel, from which all sanctities proceed, he should immediately perform some holy deed through his yearning: pray or study or perform some mitzvah. And he should make storehouses for himself in his mind, to hide there all the good of the seven good years. For a person has free choice, and he has the power, when some good yearning comes upon him, to conceal and bind it in the inwardness of his mind and take this yearning into his thought, to remember it well so that he will not forget it.

And he should make storehouses for himself in his mind, to hide there all the good of the seven good years. For a person has free choice, and he has the power, when some good yearning comes upon him, to conceal and bind it in the inwardness of his mind and take this yearning into his thought, to remember it well so that he will not forget it.

pairs.he: כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק מוֹדִיעַ לוֹ מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יָבוֹאוּ עָלָיו יְמֵי רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְיִרְצוּ לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל הַטּוֹב הַהוּא, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין מֵעַצְמוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִגְנֹז הֵיטֵב אֶת כָּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁל בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיְּקַשֵּׁר הַחֵשֶׁק דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְיִקַּח בְּדַעְתּוֹ זֶה הָעִנְיָן בְּעַצְמוֹ. שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁיִּטַּמְטֵם לִבּוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָרַע שֶׁבַּחוֹבְלִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יִתְחַזֵּק בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה׳ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַתְּשׁוּקָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כַּנַּ״ל. וְכָל הָרְשִׁימוֹת שֶׁל הַתְּשׁוּקוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מֹחוֹ יִהְיוּ לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ בִּימֵי רַע שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. בִּבְחִינַת וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן לָאָרֶץ לְשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב אֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶינָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן. וְלֹא תִכָּרֵת הָאָרֶץ בָּרָעָב כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: For since Yosef the tzaddik informs him beforehand that afterward days of evil will come upon him, God forbid, and will seek to make him forget all that good, through this the discerning person will understand on his own that he must carefully store away all the good of the aspect of the seven years of plenty. That is, he should bind the holy desire in his thought and take this very matter into his awareness: even when his heart becomes stopped up through the awakening of evil in the destroyers, nevertheless he should strengthen himself in the service of Hashem by reminding himself of the first yearning, as above. And all the impressions of the first yearnings that he stored in the inwardness of his mind will be for him a deposit to revive his soul in days of evil, which are the aspect of the seven years of famine; in the aspect of “And the food shall be for a deposit for the land for the seven years of famine that will come afterward, and the land shall not be cut off through famine,” as above.

pairs.he: עִקַּר הַבֵּרוּר הוּא בִּבְחִינַת בֵּרוּר הָאֲכִילָה וְהַשְּׂבִיעָה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת בֵּרוּר שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע מִשֶּׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב. וְעַל כֵּן נָתַן עֵצָה וַיִּצְבְּרוּ בָר וְכוּ׳ וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן.
pairs.en: The principal refinement is in the aspect of refining eating and satiation, which is the aspect of refining the seven years of plenty from the seven years of famine. Therefore he gave the counsel, “And let them amass grain,” etc., “And the food shall be held in reserve.”

pairs.he: וְאִיתָא שֶׁבָּ״ר מְרַמֵּז עַל ר״ב נִיצוֹצוֹת מֵהָרפ״ח נִיצוֹצוֹת. שֶׁבֵּרֵר יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּצְבֹּר יוֹסֵף בָּ״ר וְכוּ׳, כַּמּוּבָא קלו.
pairs.en: And it is stated that the printed expression ב״ר alludes to 202 sparks from the 288 sparks—the 202 sparks which Joseph refined in Egypt—as it is written, “And Joseph amassed בָּ״ר,” etc., as brought there [printed note marker קלו].

pairs.he: הַיְנוּ שֶׁיּוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק נוֹתֵן עֵצָה לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לָחוּס עַל נַפְשׁוֹ, שֶׁיִּקְבֹּץ אֶת כָּל אֹכֶל שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת וְכוּ׳, הַיְנוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר אֵיזֶה טוֹב בָּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע, אֲזַי יִזְדָּרֵז תֵּכֶף לִצְבֹּר וְלֶאֱסֹף אֹכֶל הַשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּמָּהֵר לַחֲטֹף תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כָּל מַה שֶׁיּוּכַל בְּעֵת הַטּוֹבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כֹּל אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא יָדְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ עֲשֵׂה וְכוּ׳, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְפִקָּדוֹן לִימֵי הָרָעָב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַיְמֵי רַע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לַעֲבֹר עַל הָאָדָם, שֶׁאָז יוּכַל לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַטּוֹב שֶׁקִּבֵּץ בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּימֵי נְעוּרָיו קלז. וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה עִקַּר קִיּוּם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹקִים לִפְנֵיכֶם לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְכוּ׳. כִּי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְכֵן כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת בִּפְרָט גָּלוּת הָאַחֲרוֹן הַמַּר הַזֶּה שֶׁכֻּלָּם מְכֻנִּים בְּשֵׁם גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, כַּמּוּבָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ, בְּכֻלָּם לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לָנוּ לְהִתְקַיֵּם לוּלֵא ה׳ עֶזְרָתָה לָנוּ שֶׁהִקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְפָנֵינוּ צַדִּיקִים נוֹרָאִים כָּאֵלֶּה שֶׁעָמְדוּ בְּנִסְיוֹנוֹת רַבִּים אֵין מִסְפָּר שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהֵם מַמְשִׁיכִים עָלֵינוּ הֶאָרוֹת מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּכַמָּה וְכַמָּה דְּרָכִים נִפְלָאִים לְהַחֲיוֹתֵנוּ כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בִּבְחִינַת לָשׂוּם לָכֶם שְׁאֵרִית בָּאָרֶץ וְלִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לִפְלֵיטָה גְּדֹלָה, אָמֵן וְאָמֵן קלח.
pairs.en: That is, Joseph the righteous gives counsel to everyone who wishes to have compassion upon his soul: he should gather all the food of the seven good years, etc. That is, when some good awakens within a person—which is the aspect of the seven years of plenty—he should immediately hasten to amass and gather the food of the good years, so that it will be held by him in reserve for the days of famine. That is, he should hasten to seize Torah, prayer, and good deeds, as much as he can during the good time, as it is written, “Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength,” etc., so that it will be held for him in reserve for the days of famine, Heaven forbid. These are the aspect of the evil days that a person must pass through, when he will be able to sustain himself with the good that he gathered at first in his youthful days [printed note marker קלז]. Therefore Israel’s principal continued existence in the Egyptian exile was through Joseph the righteous, as it is written, “For sustenance God sent me before you, to establish for you a remnant in the land,” etc. For the Egyptian exile, and likewise all the exiles—particularly this bitter final exile, all of which are called by the name of the Egyptian exile, as brought in the Midrash—in all of them it would have been impossible for us to endure had the Lord not come to our aid. He preceded the blow with its remedy by sending before us such awe-inspiring righteous men, who withstood innumerable trials, who are in the aspect of Joseph the righteous. They draw upon us illuminations from the root of our souls in the Torah, by many, many wondrous ways, to sustain us as on this day, in the aspect of “To establish for you a remnant in the land, and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.” Amen and amen [printed note marker קלח].

pairs.he: בכנפי יונה (ח״ג סימן נ״ו) כתב כן. ואחריו הביאו זה מגדולי המקובלים ז״ל. ומהם, הרמ״ז ז״ל בביאורו לזוה״ק פרשת ויקהל כתב: לבתר סטא זינא לזיניה, פי׳ שצד הרע גבר בהם. ועוד י״ל כמ״ש בכתבי הרב, כי מאותם הרפ״ח ניצוצין נכללו ר״ב בחינות מהם והיו קרובים להתקן, ונשארו פ״ו השרשיות והחזקות, ואלמלא כוונה רעה של ערב רב בשעת מתן תורה היה מתקן הכל, אבל הם גנבו שור מן המרכבה דתמן שם אלקים אחור ליפול ר״ב, וז״ש סטא זינא לזיניה, הר״ב הלך לו אצל הפ״ו. ואתי אינון ערב רב ולכן נטמעו מן הקדושה. ע״כ. והרמה״ש ז״ל בהגהות האוצרות חיים (אות ס״ג) כתב: נקדים לך הקדמה א׳ מ״ש האר״י ז״ל בפמ״א וז״ל כי רפ״ח ניצוצות שנפלו שבירי כלים שנפלו לתה״ר וכו׳ וישראל כשהיו במצרים העלה משם ר״ב ניצוצות, אבל פ״ו ניצו׳ לתשלום רפ״ח לא היה יכול מרע״ה להוציא משם מכור הברזל. וז״ש וגם ערב ר״ב עלה אתם, ר״ב דייקא ולא יותר וכו׳. שכל זה נרמז במ״ש עה״פ יעקב לבניו שמעתי כי יש שבר במצרים, שבר דייקא דהיינו על הניצוצין דשברי כלים, דדע שעמדו על פ״ו, ר״ל לא ישאר שם רק פ״ו, וזהו ושברו ׳לנו׳ גימטריא פ״ו וכו׳. וזה אפשר מש״ה ושברו לנו וכו׳ ונחיה ולא נמות, כמ״ש בכוונות האר״י זללה״ה שאלו השברים הם סיבת מיתה לבני עולם, וכשיצאו אותם השברים אז בלע המות, וזהו ׳ונחיה ולא נמות׳. ע״כ ע״ש. בעל התניא בספרו תורה אור פרשת בא (עמ׳ 120) כתב: בעצם היום הזה יצאו צבאות הוי״ה, הוא לשון סמוך שהצבאות נטפל לשם הוי״ה, אבל אינו לשון שם התואר כמ״ש הוי״ה צבאות. והיינו, בחי׳ הניצוצות שנתבררו בגלות דמצרים נתעלו ליכלל בשם הוי״ה, הם הנק׳ צבאות הוי״ה. כי רפ״ח ניצוצות נפלו בשבירת הכלים ומה נתברר בגלות מצרים ר״ב ניצוצים, וע״ז נאמר וינצלו את מצרים. וז״ש וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, וכתיב רב לך וכו׳. ע״כ. בקהלת יעקב (ערך רפ) וז״ל: רפ״ח ניצוצין מז׳ מלכין דמיתו נפלו בשברי כלים, וזה סוד ורוח אלהים מרחפת רפ״ח מת, ובמצרים העלו ר״ב ניצוצין, זה שאמר וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, זה שאמר וירדו אחי יוסף לשבור ב״ר במצרים, ופ״ו נשאר לתקן עד ביאת משיחנו, וזה שאמר ורוח אלהים וזה רוח זה רוחו של משיח נשאר לו לתקן פ״ו ניצוצין כמנין אלהים. (מפרוש תלמיד הרב על ספרא דצניעותא דף קכ״ו ע״ב). ע״כ. הפלא יועץ ז״ל בספרו עץ השדה ׳אלף המגן׳ (מפתח תולדות, מתן לך) מזכיר זאת: ויתן לך האלקים מטל השמים טל תורה מן השמים ועל ידה תוציא משמני הארץ שהם ניצוה״ק הטמונים בארץ ולא תצטרך לגלות מצרים כדי להוציא ר״ב ניצוצות כמ״ש המקובלים על פסוק וגם ערב רב עלה אתם, אלא ׳ורב׳ על ידך דגן ותירוש שהוא תשב״כ ותשבע״פ. ע״כ. ועוד טובא בספרי הצדיקים ז״ל. (עי׳ ספר ׳תכלית חכמה׳ בזה)
pairs.en: In Kanfay Yonah (part 3, section 56) he wrote thus. After him, great kabbalists of blessed memory brought this. Among them, RMZ, of blessed memory, in his explanation of the holy Zohar, the portion Vayakhel, wrote: “Afterward, a kind inclined toward its kind”—that is, the evil side prevailed within them. It may further be said, as is written in the master’s writings, that of those 288 sparks, 202 aspects of them were included and were close to being repaired, while the 86 root and strong ones remained. Were it not for the evil intention of the mixed multitude at the giving of the Torah, he would have repaired everything. But they stole the ox from the chariot, where there is the name Elokim, “backward to fall 202” [opaque phrase]; this is “a kind inclined toward its kind”: the 202 went over to the 86. “And those of the mixed multitude came,” and therefore they were submerged away from holiness. End of quotation. RMHSh, of blessed memory, in the glosses to Oatzroas Chaim (item 63), wrote: Let us preface for you one introduction, what the Ari of blessed memory wrote in PMA, in these words: For the 288 sparks that fell—broken vessels that fell to THR, etc.—and Israel, when they were in Egypt, raised 202 sparks from there. But 86 sparks, to complete the 288, Moshe Rabbainu, peace be upon him, was not able to bring out from there, from the iron furnace. This is “And also a mixed multitude—202—went up with them”: precisely 202, and no more, etc. All this is hinted at in what is written on the verse, “Yaakov, to his sons: I heard that there is grain in Egypt” [printed incipit retained]: precisely “brokenness,” meaning the sparks of the broken vessels; know that they stood at 86—that is, only 86 would remain there. This is “And buy for us”: “for us” has the numerical value 86, etc. This may be what Scripture says, “And buy for us,” etc., “and we shall live and not die,” as is written in the Ari’s intentions, may his memory be for the life of the World to Come, that these fragments cause death for the people of the world; when those fragments go out, then “He has swallowed up death.” This is “and we shall live and not die.” End of quotation; see there. The author of Tanya, in his book Torah Oar, the portion Bo (p. 120), wrote: “On this very day the hosts of the Divine Name went out” is a construct expression: the hosts are subordinate to the Divine Name; it is not an expression of a descriptive name, as in “the Divine Name of Hosts.” That is, the sparks refined in the Egyptian exile were elevated to be included in the Divine Name; they are called “the hosts of the Divine Name.” For 288 sparks fell in the breaking of the vessels, and what was refined in the Egyptian exile was 202 sparks. Concerning this it was said, “And they emptied Egypt.” This is “And also a mixed multitude went up with them,” and it is written, “It is much for you,” etc. End of quotation. In Kihilas Yaakov (entry רפ), in these words: The 288 sparks from the seven kings who died fell in the fragments of vessels. This is the secret of “And the spirit of God was hovering”: 288, dead. In Egypt they raised 202 sparks. This is what it says, “And also a mixed multitude went up with them”; this is what it says, “And Yosef’s brothers descended to buy grain”—BR—in Egypt. And 86 remained to be repaired until the coming of our Messiah. This is what it says, “And the spirit of God”: this spirit is the spirit of the Messiah; it remains for him to repair 86 sparks, the numerical value of Elokim. (From the explanation of the master’s disciple on Sifra DiTzneeoosuh, folio 126, side b.) End of quotation. The Pele Yoetz, of blessed memory, in his book Aitz HaSudeh, “Elef HaMugen” (index of Toaldoas, “grant you”), mentions this: “And God shall grant you of the dew of heaven”—the dew of Torah from heaven; through it you shall bring out of the fatness of the earth, which are the holy sparks hidden in the earth, and you will not have to go into Egyptian exile to bring out 202 sparks, as the kabbalists wrote on the verse “And also a mixed multitude went up with them,” but “abundant” grain and wine through you, which is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. End of quotation. There is much more in the books of the righteous, of blessed memory. (See the book Tachlis Chokhmah concerning this.)

pairs.he: המגיד מקאזניץ ז״ל כתב בעבודת ישראל (יום ב׳ דפסח) כתב: כתוב אומר (קהלת ז יד) ביום טובה היה בטוב וביום רעה ראה, דהיינו שיש באדם מוחין דגדלות השעות שיוכל לעבוד את בוראו בבהירות ובהתלהבות, ויש עתים וזמן שמסתלק ממנו המוחין ונשאר בקטנות. והכלל, שצריך האדם לזכור בשעת מוחין דגדלות, להכין עצמו ולעשות רושם בקרבו, הגם שיסתלק ממנו ההתלהבות – לא יפול לגמרי ח״ו, ויהיה מהנצחים קרבא ויתחזק וישען בה׳. וכן בכל הזמנים, למשל בשבתות וימים טובים שאז זמן התלהבות בחשק נפלא לעבודתו יתברך שמו, צריך האדם להכין עצמו על ימי החול הבאים שיהיה מקושר גם כן בבוראו ית״ש. וכן ביום א׳ דפסח אמרו רז״ל הסימן את״ב א״ת ב״ש, א״ת – א׳ דפסח הוא תשעה באב. ואם כן צריך האדם לקשר עצמו ביום א׳ דפסח הטיב בבוראו, עד שאפילו בט׳ באב שהוא יום הירידה מכל המדרגות, יהיה גם כן מקושר בעבודת השי״ת, וזה רמז ׳ביום טובה היה בטוב׳, וגם אז ראה והבט על יום רעה, כשבא ירידת המוחין הכן עצמך עליו שלא תפול בו. ע״כ. וכן הוא בדבריו בדרוש לחנוכה: תמיד צריך האדם להכין קדושה מימים טובים על ימים הנמוכים וכמו שבארתי בפסוק ביום טובה היה בטוב וביום רעה ראה. וכמו שקבלנו מרבינו מורינו אלימלך זצ״ל בספרו הקדוש ׳אמור ואמרת׳ להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים, שמימי מוחין דגדלות צריך להיות הכנה על ימין דמוחין דקטנות. ע״כ.
pairs.en: The Maggid of Kozhnitz, of blessed memory, wrote in Avoadas Yisrael (the second day of Passover), wrote: Scripture says (Ecclesiastes 7:14), “On a day of good be in good, and on a day of evil see.” That is, a person has mental faculties in an expanded state—the hours when he can serve his Creator with clarity and ardor—and there are times and a season when the mental faculties withdraw from him and he remains in a constricted state. The general principle is that, at the time of expanded mental faculties, a person must remember to prepare himself and make an impression within himself, so that, even though the ardor withdraws from him, he will not fall completely, Heaven forbid, but will be among those who prevail in battle, strengthen himself, and rely on God. So too at all times; for example, on Sabbaths and festivals, when it is a time of ardor with wondrous desire for His service, blessed be His name, a person must prepare himself for the coming weekdays, so that he will also be bound to his Creator, blessed be His name. Thus, concerning the first day of Passover, our Sages of blessed memory stated the mnemonic AT-B, AT-BSh: AT—the first day of Passover is the Ninth of Av. Accordingly, on the first day of Passover a person must bind himself well to his Creator, so that even on the Ninth of Av, which is a day of descent from all levels, he will also be bound to the service of the blessed God. This is what “On a day of good be in good” hints at: even then, see and look toward a day of evil, when the withdrawal of the mental faculties comes, prepare yourself for it, so that you will not fall in it. End of quotation. Likewise, in his words in the discourse for Hanukkah: a person must always prepare holiness from festivals for the lowly days, as I explained on the verse “On a day of good be in good, and on a day of evil see.” And as we received from our master and teacher, Elimelech, of blessed righteous memory, in his holy book: “Say, and you shall say”—to admonish the great concerning the small; from days of expanded mental faculties there must be preparation for days of constricted mental faculties. End of quotation.

pairs.he: וז״ל החיד״א בכסא דוד (דרוש כ״ה לשבת הגדול) וכל ביאת יוסף למצרים היה הכנה שיבואו ישראל ויבררו ניצוה״ק של אדה״ר, ויוסף הצדיק בחינת נפשו סבל עבדות והיה מסלול ודרך הקדוש לגאולת ישראל, כי הוא בחי׳ אדה״ר. ומזה תשכיל כי הסט״א נתלבשה באשת פוטיפר והשתדלה מאד להחטיא את יוסף, כי בזה תלוי הכנעת הס״א שישראל יוציאו בלעם וניצוה״ק, או להיפך אם ח״ו יוסף הצדיק היה חוטא ח״ו היה נפגם היסוד הק׳ ובחי׳ אדה״ר ר״ל ולא היה עוד תקומה לישראל ח״ו. והשתא ניחא כל מרבית פיתויים והסתות אשר מעולם לא היו, כי הס״א עשתה כל מאמצי כחה בכמה מיני אופני הטעאות ועיונים ליוסף הצדיק ע״ה כמי שרודף אחר חייו. והוא היה סיבה עיקרית ליציאת מצרים, בהיותו ניצו׳ אדה״ר והפליא לעשות וניצול מאשת פוטיפר, והיה עבד לכפר עבדות ישראל ויסוד מוסד לגאולה העתידה. ע״כ. המאור ושמש בפרשת ויגש כתב: היה הקב״ה מסבב סיבובים במכירת יוסף דוקא שהוא סוד צדיק שומר הברית דוקא למצרים שהוא דבר והיפוכו אבי אבות הטומאה ערות הארץ שטופי זימה ושם ניסה הקב״ה אותו באשת פוטיפר ועמד בנסיון ולא פגם את אות ברית קודש, וזאת בלתי אפשרי היה באיזה משאר האחים כי אולי לא עמדו בנסיונם, ודוקא יוסף הצדיק שהוא סוד צדיק שומר הברית הוא יכול לעמוד בנסיון זה בשמירת הברית והוא המשיך דבר זה למצרים שהתחיל לתקן שם תיקון הברית מפגימת אדם הראשון. ומעשה אבות סימן לבנים שבעקבותיו דרכו אחר כך בני ישראל בארץ מצרים בגדירת הערוה שגדרו עצמם ועשו התיקון הזה בשלימות בתיקון שמירת הברית והעלו כל הניצוצצים עד שעשאו כמצולה שאין בה דגים, וחלת יוסף המשיך זאת לא היה כח ביד בני ישראל למשוך ולתקן זאת רק על ידי המשכת יוסף הצדיק היו יכולים אחר כך בני ישראל לתקן זאת עד ששרשו והיו יכולים לעלות ממצרים והיה הגאולה על ידי יוסף על ידי שהתחיל להמשיך דבר זה. וזהו שאיתא במדרש על פסוק הים ראה וינס ארונו של יוסף ראה כו׳. ע״כ. בבאר מים חיים פרשת מקץ: נודע אשר כל עיקר ירידת יוסף למצרים לא היה אלא בכדי ליישר דרך לפני בני ישראל, כאשר יבואו לגור במצרים לעבוד ולמשא שיוכלו להתקיים שם ולצאת משם שלא ישקעו נפשותם בטומאת וזוהמת מצרים בנ׳ שערים שבה, ששוב לא היו יכולים לצאת משם לעולם כו׳. והעיקר שבד׳ דברים הללו הוא, שהיו גדורים מן העריות ומפורש עליהם בקבלה גן נעול אחותי כלה גל נעול וגו׳ ואמרו חז״ל גן נעול אלו הזכרים גל נעול אלו הנקבות ובני ישראל ירדו למצרים ובני ישראל עלו ושבטי יה עדות לישראל שלא היו רק כשרי בני ישראל כמאמרם חז״ל. ודבר זה עלה לפני המקום ברוך הוא ביותר ויותר כי אחרי שמצרים שטופי זימה הם כאומרם ז״ל כי קליפת מצרים גובר מאוד לתאוה ההיא ביותר שעל כן נקרא ערות הארץ ששם התגברות קליפה זו, ואף על פי כן נשמרו ישראל מכל רע הלזה ולא היה להם עדיין אף קבלת התורה להיות להתבלין ליצר הרע. ואז יוסף הצדיק בצדקתו הוא כבש דרך הזה לפני בני ישראל, בעומדו בנסיון באשת אדוניו, והכניע הקליפה ההיא לפני בני ישראל. באופן שכאשר יתעצמו בני ישראל בדבר הזה יוכלו להתגבר בזה על תאותם לנעול דלת בפני לבן הארמי זר לא יקרב אליהם כי קדש הם. ע״כ.
pairs.en: And these are the words of the Chida in Keesay Dovid (discourse 25 for the Great Sabbath): Yosef’s entire coming to Egypt was preparation so that Israel would come and refine the holy sparks of Adam the first man. Yosef the righteous—the aspect of his soul—bore servitude and was a path and the holy way for Israel’s redemption, for he is an aspect of Adam the first man. From this you will understand that the Other Side clothed itself in Potiphar’s wife and strove very much to cause Yosef to sin, for upon this depends the subjugation of the Other Side, that Israel should extract what they swallowed and the holy sparks; or, conversely, if, Heaven forbid, Yosef the righteous had sinned, Heaven forbid, the holy foundation and the aspect of Adam the first man would have been damaged, Heaven spare us, and there would no longer have been any recovery for Israel, Heaven forbid. Now all the abundance of enticements and incitements that had never existed becomes understandable, for the Other Side exerted all its strength through many kinds of means of deception and speculations, against Yosef the righteous, peace be upon him, like one who pursues his life. He was a principal cause of the departure from Egypt, being a spark of Adam the first man; he did wondrously and was saved from Potiphar’s wife, and was a servant to atone for Israel’s servitude and an established foundation for the future redemption. End of quotation. HaMuoar VuShemesh, in the portion Vayigash, wrote: The Holy One, blessed be He, was bringing about turns of events in the sale of precisely Yosef, who is the secret of a righteous one who guards the covenant, precisely to Egypt, which is the thing and its opposite—the primary source of impurity, the nakedness of the land, steeped in lewdness. There the Holy One, blessed be He, tested him with Potiphar’s wife, and he withstood the trial and did not damage the sign of the holy covenant. This would have been impossible for any of the other brothers, for perhaps they would not have withstood their trial. Precisely Yosef the righteous, who is the secret of a righteous one who guards the covenant, can withstand this trial through guarding the covenant. He drew this matter into Egypt, beginning to repair there the repair of the covenant from Adam the first man’s damage. “The deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children”: afterward the children of Israel walked in his footsteps in the land of Egypt by fencing off sexual transgression, fencing themselves off and carrying out this repair completely through repairing the guarding of the covenant. They raised all the sparks until they made it like a deep pool with no fish in it. “And the sickness of Yosef drew this” [candidate wording]: the children of Israel would not have had the strength to draw and repair this except through Yosef the righteous drawing it; afterward the children of Israel could repair this until they rooted it and could ascend from Egypt. The redemption was through Yosef, by his beginning to draw this matter. This is what is stated in the Midrash on the verse “The sea saw and fled”: it saw Yosef’s coffin, etc. End of quotation. In Biair Mayim Chaim, the portion Miketz: It is known that the whole essence of Yosef’s descent into Egypt was only to straighten a path before the children of Israel when they would come to dwell in Egypt for labor and burdens, so that they could endure there and leave there, and their souls would not sink into Egypt’s impurity and filth, into its fifty gates, from which they would no longer be able to emerge forever, etc. The principal thing in these four matters is that they were fenced off from sexual transgressions; and it is stated explicitly about them in the scriptural tradition, “A locked garden, my sister, bride; a locked spring,” etc. Our Sages of blessed memory said: “A locked garden”—these are the males; “a locked spring”—these are the females. And the children of Israel descended into Egypt and the children of Israel ascended; and “the tribes of Yah, a testimony to Israel”, that they were only the fit children of Israel, as our Sages of blessed memory stated. This matter rose before the Omnipresent, blessed be He, exceedingly, for since the Egyptians are steeped in lewdness, as they of blessed memory say, since the husk of Egypt prevails very greatly toward that desire; therefore it is called “the nakedness of the land,” for that is where this husk prevails. Nevertheless, Israel guarded themselves from every such evil, and they did not yet even have the receiving of the Torah to serve as a seasoning for the evil inclination. Yosef the righteous, in his righteousness, then paved this path before the children of Israel by withstanding the trial with his master’s wife and subduing that husk before the children of Israel. Thus, when the children of Israel would exert themselves in this matter, they could prevail in it over their desire, to lock the door before Lavan the Aramean; a stranger would not come near them, for they are holy. End of quotation.

pairs.he: על ידי שיוסף עמד בנסיון שם ומצא את הטוב כל מקום, עי״ז עמדו ישראל אח״כ שם
pairs.en: Through Yosef withstanding the trial there and finding the good in every place, through this Israel subsequently stood there.

qualifiedAfter.en: Through Yosef withstanding the trial there and finding the good in every place, through this Israel subsequently stood there.

pairs.he: ״וַיִּקְרָא יוֹסֵף אֶת שֵׁם הַבְּכוֹר מְנַשֶּׁה וְגוֹ׳״

pairs.he: עַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָאִים בְּנֵי יוֹסֵף מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶפְרָיִם, עַל שֶׁהוֹלִידָם יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהוּא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ וְהוּא בְּגֹדֶל צִדְקָתוֹ זָכָה גַּם שָׁם לַעֲמֹד בְּנִסָּיוֹן וּלְבַלִּי לִפֹּל בְּדַעְתּוֹ בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו, שֶׁזֶּהוּ גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל הַנִּסָּיוֹן.
pairs.en: On this account Yosef’s sons are called Menasheh and Ephraim: because Yosef begot them in Egypt, which is the nakedness of the land, and, through the greatness of his righteousness, he merited to withstand the trial even there and not to become discouraged through everything that befell him, which is also included in the trial.

qualifiedAfter.en: On this account Yosef’s sons are called Menasheh and Ephraim: because Yosef begot them in Egypt, which is the nakedness of the land, and, through the greatness of his righteousness, he merited to withstand the trial even there and not to become discouraged through everything that befell him, which is also included in the trial.

pairs.he: כִּי כְּשֶׁמְּנַסִּין אֶת הָאָדָם לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת שְׁלֵמוּת הַדַּעַת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקַּר הַנִּסָּיוֹן, כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּיו זכרונו לברכה. וְיוֹסֵף עָבַר עָלָיו כָּל זֶה וְהָיָה בְּנִסָּיוֹן גָּדוֹל וְעָמַד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְבָרֵר וְלִמְצֹא הַטּוֹב בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה כֹּחַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת בְּמִצְרַיִם בַּגָּלוּת, כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחוֹ אֱלֹקִים.
pairs.en: For when a person is tested, the completeness of awareness is taken from him; this is the essence of the trial, as I heard from his mouth, of blessed memory. All this befell Yosef, and he was in a great trial and withstood the trial. Through this he merited to have the strength to refine and find the good wherever he was. Through this Israel had the strength to be in Egypt in exile, for God sent him to preserve life.

qualifiedAfter.en: For when a person is tested, the completeness of awareness is taken from him; this is the essence of the trial, as I heard from his mouth, of blessed memory. All this befell Yosef, and he was in a great trial and withstood the trial. Through this he merited to have the strength to refine and find the good wherever he was. Through this Israel had the strength to be in Egypt in exile, for God sent him to preserve life.

pairs.he: כִּי לוּלֵא כֹּחַ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהִקְדִּים לִפְנֵיהֶם שָׁם, לֹא הָיָה כֹּחַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲמֹד בַּגָּלוּת. וְכֵן עַכְשָׁו לוּלֵא כֹּחַ הַצַּדִּיקִים הָאֲמִתִּיִּים שֶׁמְּלַמְּדִים עָלֵינוּ זְכוּת וּמְחַזְּקִים אוֹתָנוּ עַל פִּי הַדְּרָכִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַנַּ״ל קלט, לֹא הָיָה כֹּחַ לִסְבֹּל מְרִירוּת הַגָּלוּת בִּכְלָלִיּוּת, וּבִפְרָט הַגָּלוּת שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
pairs.en: For were it not for the strength of Yosef the righteous, who preceded them there, Israel would not have had the strength to endure the exile. Likewise now, were it not for the strength of the true righteous ones, who plead merit on our behalf and strengthen us according to the aforementioned holy paths [printed note marker 139], there would not be the strength to bear the bitterness of exile in general, and especially the exile of each and every individual.

qualifiedAfter.en: For were it not for the strength of Yosef the righteous, who preceded them there, Israel would not have had the strength to endure the exile. Likewise now, were it not for the strength of the true righteous ones, who plead merit on our behalf and strengthen us according to the aforementioned holy paths [printed note marker 139], there would not be the strength to bear the bitterness of exile in general, and especially the exile of each and every individual.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן קָרָא שֵׁם בָּנָיו מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶפְרָיִם, עַל שֵׁם זֶה שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בַּמְּקוֹמוֹת הָרְחוֹקִים מְאֹד יְכוֹלִים לִמְצֹא אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי כָּל הַנַּ״ל. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם ״כִּי נַשַּׁנִי אֶת כָּל עֲמָלִי וְכוּ׳״, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ הַנִּשָּׁיוֹן וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הַכֹּל מֵה׳.
pairs.en: And therefore he called the names of his sons Menasheh and Ephraim, on account of this: that even in very distant places one can find the blessed God through all the foregoing. This is the aspect of Menasheh, who was named for “For He has made me forget all my toil,” etc.: even the trial and the forgetting are all from God.

qualifiedAfter.en: And therefore he called the names of his sons Menasheh and Ephraim, on account of this: that even in very distant places one can find the blessed God through all the foregoing. This is the aspect of Menasheh, who was named for “For He has made me forget all my toil,” etc.: even the trial and the forgetting are all from God.

pairs.he: הַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם בִּבְחִינַת חָלָל הַפָּנוּי שֶׁשָּׁם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לִמְצֹא אֱלֹקוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, גַּם זֶה מֵה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַנִּשָּׁיוֹן וְהַשִּׁכְחָה גַּם כֵּן מֵה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל וּלְחַפֵּשׂ אֶת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם מִשָּׁם כַּנַּ״ל. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת אַיֵּה הַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: That is, even in the aspect of the vacated space, where one cannot find His divinity, blessed be He, this too is from the blessed God; for he knows that the trial and the forgetting are also from the blessed God. Through this he can endeavor and search for the blessed God even from there, as explained above. This is the aforementioned aspect of “Where?”

qualifiedAfter.en: That is, even in the aspect of the vacated space, where one cannot find His divinity, blessed be He, this too is from the blessed God; for he knows that the trial and the forgetting are also from the blessed God. Through this he can endeavor and search for the blessed God even from there, as explained above. This is the aforementioned aspect of “Where?”

pairs.he: וְאֶפְרַיִם נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם כִּי הִפְרַנִי אֱלֹקִים בְּאֶרֶץ עָנְיִי, שֶׁגַּם בְּאֶרֶץ עָנְיִי אֲנִי יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא טוֹב, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת פֵּרוֹת וְיִזְרְעוּ שָׂדוֹת וְיִטְּעוּ כְרָמִים כַּנַּ״ל. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁל אַזְמְרָה הַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And Ephraim is named for “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction”: even in the land of my affliction I can find good, which is the aspect of fruit, “And they shall sow fields and plant vineyards,” as explained above. This is the aspect of the aforementioned path of “I shall sing.”

pairs.he: א) זה בחינת מה שכתוב במדרש (מדרש רבה פרשת מקץ פרק צא) וזה לשונו, וַיַּרְא יַעֲקֹב כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר בְּמִצְרַיִם. כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר זֶה הָרָעָב, כִּי יֵשׁ סֶבֶר זֶה הַשָּׂבָע, כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר וְיוֹסֵף הוּרַד מִצְרַיְמָה, כִּי יֵשׁ סֶבֶר וְיוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט, כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אוֹתָם, כִּי יֵשׁ סֶבֶר וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל. ׳הָאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְכוּ׳ וּבְעַד כּוֹכָבִים יַחְתֹּם׳, אֵלּוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁהָיוּ נִכְנָסִים וְיוֹצְאִים לְמִצְרַיִם וְלֹא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִים שֶׁיוֹסֵף קַיָּם, עַד כָּאן לְשׁוֹן הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
pairs.en: a) This is the aspect of what is written in the Midrash (Midrash Rabbah, the portion Miketz, chapter 91), in these words: “And Yaakov saw that there was shever in Egypt.” “For there is shever”—this is the famine; “for there is sever”—this is the plenty. “For there is shever”—“And Yosef was brought down to Egypt”; “for there is sever”—“And Yosef was the ruler.” “For there is shever”—“And they shall enslave them and afflict them”; “for there is sever”—“And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” “Who speaks to the sun,” etc., “and seals off the stars”—these are the ten tribes who were entering and leaving Egypt and did not know that Yosef was alive. Thus far the words of the Midrash.

pairs.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁדּוֹרֵשׁ ״שֶׁבֶר״ לְשׁוֹן סֶבֶר וְתִקְוָה, הַיְנוּ עִנְיָן הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁהַהִתְרַחֲקוּת הוּא הַהִתְקָרְבוּת, וְהָאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מְצַפֶּה לִישׁוּעָה תָּמִיד. וּבְתוֹךְ הַצָּרָה וְהַדַּחֲקוּת וְגֹדֶל צָרַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְגָלוּתָהּ כְּפִי שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ כָּל אֶחָד בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, צָרִיךְ לִרְאוֹת וּלְהִסְתַּכֵּל מִשָּׁם דַּיְקָא תִּקְוָה וְסֶבֶר לִגְאֻלַּת נַפְשׁוֹ לָשׁוּב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
pairs.en: It follows that he interprets “shever” as an expression of sever and hope. This is the aforementioned matter: that distancing is the drawing near. And an Israelite, the aspect of Yaakov, must always anticipate salvation. Within distress and straits, and the great distress of the soul and its exile, as each individual feels in his soul, one must see and look precisely from there for hope and expectation for the redemption of his soul, to return to Him, blessed be He.

pairs.he: בִּבְחִינַת וַיַּרְא יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר בְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי יֵשׁ סֶבֶר וְתִקְוָה בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם דַּיְקָא שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תֹּקֶף הַגָּלוּת בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט, כִּי כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת מְכֻנִּים בְּשֵׁם מִצְרַיִם, שָׁם דַּיְקָא בְּתוֹךְ הַשֶּׁבֶר וְהַצָּרָה יֵשׁ סֶבֶר וְתִקְוָה גְדוֹלָה כַּנַּ״ל בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבֶר וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אוֹתָם, כִּי יֵשׁ סֶבֶר וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל.
pairs.en: In the aspect of “And Yaakov saw”—he being an Israelite—“that there was shever in Egypt”: that there is expectation and hope in Egypt. Precisely in Egypt, which is the aspect of the intensity of exile in general and in particular—for all exiles are designated by the name Egypt—there, precisely within the breaking and distress, there is great expectation and hope, as explained above in the Midrash. For there is shever: “And they shall enslave them and afflict them”; there is sever: “And afterward they shall go out with great possessions.”

pairs.he: וְכֵן הוּא בַּגָּלוּת שֶׁל עַכְשָׁו וְכֵן הוּא בְּכָל אָדָם בִּפְרָטִיּוּת שֶׁכָּל זֶה הוּא בְּחִינַת שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב שֶׁהַהִתְרַחֲקוּת הוּא עִקַּר הַהִתְקָרְבוּת וְכַנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: So it is in the present exile, and so it is in each person individually: all this is the aspect of “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,” for the distancing is the essence of the drawing near, as explained above.

pairs.he: כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת וְכָל הַבְּרָכוֹת נִמְשָׁכִין מֵהַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת וְיוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת וְכָל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת, בְּחִינַת וְיוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט עַל הָאָרֶץ הוּא הַמַּשְׁבִּיר לְכָל עַם הָאָרֶץ. כִּי הַצַּדִּיק בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הוּא בְּחִינַת שָׂבָע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיעַ וּמְבַטֵּל שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת חֶרְפָּה בְּחִינַת חֶרְפַּת רָעָב, כַּמּוּבָא בְּדִבְרֵי רבנו זכרונו לברכה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, כִּי יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק הוּא זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם בִּשְׁנֵי הָרָעָב, כִּי הוּא מְבַטֵּל חֶרְפַּת רָעָב, בִּבְחִינַת ׳אָסַף אֱלֹקִים אֶת חֶרְפָּתִי׳ הַנֶּאֱמַר בְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק. כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט הוּא הַמַּשְׁבִּיר וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: All flows of bounty and all blessings are drawn from the righteous one, who is the aspect of “And Yosef was the ruler,” who is the source of all blessings and all flows of bounty—the aspect of “And Yosef was the ruler over the land; he was the one providing grain for all the people of the land.” For the righteous one, the aspect of Yosef, is the aspect of the seven years of plenty; he subdues and nullifies the seven years of famine, which are the aspect of disgrace, the aspect of the disgrace of famine, as is brought in the words of our master, of blessed memory, elsewhere. For Yosef the righteous nourishes and sustains the whole world in the years of famine, because he nullifies the disgrace of famine, in the aspect of “God has gathered away my disgrace,” said concerning Yosef the righteous. For “Yosef was the ruler; he was the one providing grain,” etc., as explained above.

pairs.he: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם פַּרְעֹה לְכוּ אֶל יוֹסֵף אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר לָכֶם תַּעֲשׂוּ וּפֵרֵשׁ רש״י שֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ שֶׁגַּם הֵם אָצְרוּ תְּבוּאָה וְהִרְקִיבָה, אָמַר לָהֶם, אִם כֵּן אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר לָכֶם תַּעֲשׂוּ, כִּי יוֹסֵף אָמַר לָהֶם שֶׁיִּמּוֹלוּ וְכוּ׳. הֲלֹא גָּזַר עַל הַתְּבוּאָה וְהִרְקִיבָה מַה אִם יִגְזֹר עָלֵינוּ וְנָמוּת וְכוּ׳. כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיעַ חֶרְפַּת רָעָב כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת מִילָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַבְּרִית שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ נִתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק מוֹשֵׁל בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And this is what Pharaoh told them: “Go to Yosef; do whatever he tells you.” Rashi explained that they told him that they too had stored grain, but it rotted. He told them: “If so, do whatever he tells you,” for Yosef told them to circumcise themselves, etc. “Did he not decree concerning the grain, and it rotted? What if he decrees concerning us, and we die?” etc. For it is impossible to subdue the disgrace of famine except through the aspect of circumcision, which is the aspect of repairing the covenant, through which the light of the holy point is revealed—the aspect of “a righteous one rules,” the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” as explained above.

He told them: “If so, do whatever he tells you,” for Yosef told them to circumcise themselves, etc. “Did he not decree concerning the grain, and it rotted? What if he decrees concerning us, and we die?” etc. For it is impossible to subdue the disgrace of famine except through the aspect of circumcision, which is the aspect of repairing the covenant, through which the light of the holy point is revealed—the aspect of “a righteous one rules,” the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” as explained above.

pairs.he: וְזֶהוּ הֲלֹא גָּזַר עַל הַתְּבוּאָה וְהִרְקִיבָה, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק מוֹשֵׁל, בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט וְיִגְזֹר אֹמֶר וַיָּקָם. כִּי כָּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְקָרֵב עַצְמוֹ אֶל אוֹר הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הוּא רָחוֹק מִבְּרָכָה וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הָרָעָב וְעַל כֵּן הַתְּבוּאָה נִרְקֶבֶת אֶצְלָם וְכַנַּ״ל. מַה אִם יִגְזֹר עָלֵינוּ וְנָמוּת, כִּי כָּל הַחִיּוּת הוּא רַק מֵהַצַּדִּיק מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק חַי עָלְמִין וּבִלְעָדָיו אֵין שׁוּם חִיּוּת בָּעוֹלָם רַק מַה שֶּׁמְּקַבְּלִין חִיּוּת מֵהַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַנְּקֻדָּה הַנַּ״ל, שֶׁמְּחַיֶּה וּמְבַטֵּל שְׁבִירַת לֵב שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת סִטְרָא דְמוֹתָא כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְהַצַּדִּיק מְבַטֵּל בְּחִינַת שְׁבִירַת לֵב וּמַמְשִׁיךְ חִיּוּת בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי שָׁם צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה חַיִּים וְכוּ׳ כַּיָּדוּעַ.
pairs.en: And this is “Did he not decree concerning the grain, and it rotted?” For he is the aspect of “a righteous one rules,” the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” and “he shall decree a matter, and it shall be established.” For whoever does not bring himself close to the light of the holy point is distant from blessing; the aspect of the seven years of famine prevails over him, and therefore their grain rots, as explained above. “What if he decrees concerning us, and we die?” For all vitality comes only from the righteous one, from the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of the righteous one, the life of the worlds. Without him there is no vitality at all in the world, except what vitality is received from the righteous one, who is the aforementioned aspect of the light of the point, which gives life and nullifies brokenheartedness, which is the aspect of the side of death, as is known. The righteous one nullifies the aspect of brokenheartedness and draws vitality into the world, for “There God commanded the blessing, life,” etc., as is known.

qualifiedAfter.en: And this is “Did he not decree concerning the grain, and it rotted?” For he is the aspect of “a righteous one rules,” the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” and “he shall decree a matter, and it shall be established.” For whoever does not bring himself close to the light of the holy point is distant from blessing; the aspect of the seven years of famine prevails over him, and therefore their grain rots, as explained above. “What if he decrees concerning us, and we die?” For all vitality comes only from the righteous one, from the aspect of Yosef, the aspect of the righteous one, the life of the worlds. Without him there is no vitality at all in the world, except what vitality is received from the righteous one, who is the aforementioned aspect of the light of the point, which gives life and nullifies brokenheartedness, which is the aspect of the side of death, as is known. The righteous one nullifies the aspect of brokenheartedness and draws vitality into the world, for “There God commanded the blessing, life,” etc., as is known.

pairs.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה אֵיזֶה בְּרָכָה וְהַשְׁפָּעָה לְבַטֵּל חֶרְפַּת רָעָב, הוּא צָרִיךְ לָבוֹא אֶל יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק בְּחִינַת אוֹר הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, בִּבְחִינַת ׳וְכָל הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה אֶל יוֹסֵף לִשְׁבֹּר׳ וְכוּ׳ וַאֲפִלּוּ יַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת וְעַמֵּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְקַבֵּל הַשֶּׁפַע וְהַבְּרָכָה לְבַטֵּל שֶׁבֶר רַעֲבוֹן בִּבְחִינָתָם, כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה הַכְּלָלִיּוּת שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה צְרִיכִין הַכֹּל לְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ כַּנַּ״ל. וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֶחָד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִנֵּהּ וּבֵהּ. אֲבָל בַּתְּחִלָּה צְרִיכִין הַכֹּל לְקַבֵּל דַּיְקָא מֵהַצַּדִּיק מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף וְכוּ׳. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא נִתְבַּטְּלִין הַחֲרָפוֹת הַשּׁוֹרִין עַל הַלֵּב שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת אַהֲבוֹת הַנְּפוּלִין שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת חֶרְפַּת רָעָב. כִּי עִקַּר הָרְעָבוֹן הוּא לַבְּהֵמִיּוּת, הַיְנוּ מֵחֲמַת אַהֲבוֹת הַנְּפוּלִין, אַהֲבַת הַבְּהֵמִיּוּת, מִשָּׁם עִקַּר הָרְעָבוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת חֶרְפַּת רָעָב ׳חֶרְפָּה׳ דַּיְקָא כַּנַּ״ל וְכַמְבֹאָר בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
pairs.en: And anyone who wants any blessing and flow of bounty to nullify the disgrace of famine must come to Yosef, who is the aspect of the righteous one, the aspect of the light of the holy point, in the aspect of “And all the land came to Egypt, to Yosef, to buy grain,” etc. Even Yaakov and his sons, who are the aspect of “And your people Israel are all righteous,” nevertheless cannot receive the bounty and blessing to nullify the breaking of hunger in their aspect, except through the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” who is the aspect of the general point, the root of the souls of Israel. At first everyone must receive from him, as explained above; afterward, one from his fellow; afterward, from and within himself. But at first everyone must receive precisely from the righteous one, from the aspect of Yosef, etc. Precisely through this, the disgraces resting upon the heart are nullified; they are the aspect of fallen loves, the aspect of the disgrace of famine. For the essential hunger is for animality—that is, because of fallen loves, the love of animality. From there comes the essential hunger, which is the aspect of the disgrace of famine—specifically “disgrace,” as explained above and as explained in our master’s words elsewhere.

qualifiedAfter.en: And anyone who wants any blessing and flow of bounty to nullify the disgrace of famine must come to Yosef, who is the aspect of the righteous one, the aspect of the light of the holy point, in the aspect of “And all the land came to Egypt, to Yosef, to buy grain,” etc. Even Yaakov and his sons, who are the aspect of “And your people Israel are all righteous,” nevertheless cannot receive the bounty and blessing to nullify the breaking of hunger in their aspect, except through the aspect of “Yosef was the ruler,” who is the aspect of the general point, the root of the souls of Israel. At first everyone must receive from him, as explained above; afterward, one from his fellow; afterward, from and within himself. But at first everyone must receive precisely from the righteous one, from the aspect of Yosef, etc. Precisely through this, the disgraces resting upon the heart are nullified; they are the aspect of fallen loves, the aspect of the disgrace of famine. For the essential hunger is for animality—that is, because of fallen loves, the love of animality. From there comes the essential hunger, which is the aspect of the disgrace of famine—specifically “disgrace,” as explained above and as explained in our master’s words elsewhere.

pairs.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לָהֶם יַעֲקֹב לְכוּ הָבִיאוּ שֶׁבֶר רַעֲבוֹן בָּתֵּיכֶם. ׳שֶׁבֶר׳ דַּיְקָא. כִּי עִקַּר הָרְעָבוֹן מִבְּחִינַת שְׁבִירַת לֵב. בְּחִינַת חֶרְפָּה שָׁבְרָה לִבִּי, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת חֶרְפַּת רָעָב וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל שֶׁהִתְקַנּוּ עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף דַּיְקָא כַּנַּ״ל שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ עִקַּר הַשְּׂבִיעָה בִּבְחִינַת וַאֲכַלְתֶּם לַחְמְכֶם לַשֹּׂבַע, שֶׁתִּשְׁלַח בְּרָכָה בְּמֵעַיִם בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק אוֹכֵל לְשֹׂבַע נַפְשׁוֹ.
pairs.en: And this is the aspect of what Yaakov told them: “Go, bring food for the hunger of your households”—specifically “shever.” For the essence of hunger is from the aspect of brokenheartedness, the aspect of “Disgrace has broken my heart,” which is the aspect of the disgrace of famine, etc., as explained above, repaired precisely through Yosef, as explained above. Through him comes the essential satiation, in the aspect of “And you shall eat your bread to satiation,” so that blessing will be sent into the innards, the aspect of “A righteous one eats to satisfy his soul.”

pairs.he: כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת וְכָל הַשְּׂבִיעָה נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נָהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת וְכוּ׳, כִּי כָּל הַדְּבָרִים כֻּלָּם נִמְשָׁכִין מֵאַרְבָּעָה יְסוֹדוֹת שֶׁכֻּלָּם נִמְשָׁכִין מֵהַצַּדִּיק וְכוּ׳ כַּנַּ״ל, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת וְנָהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגַּן כַּנַּ״ל, כִּי הַצַּדִּיק מַשְׁקֶה וּמַרְוֶה אֶת הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת, כִּי כָּל הַגֶּשֶׁם וְהַמָּטָר יוֹרְדִין עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר ה׳ עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאָדָם אַיִן וְכוּ׳. שֶׁהוּא הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ כָּל הַמָּטָר לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת נָהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת וְכוּ׳ וּמִשָּׁם יִפָּרֵד וְכוּ׳.
pairs.en: All flows of bounty and all satiation are drawn from the righteous one of the generation, the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of a river coming out of Eden to water, etc. For absolutely all things are drawn from four elements, all of which are drawn from the righteous one, etc., as explained above. He is the aspect of “And a river comes out of Eden to water the garden,” as explained above, for the righteous one waters and saturates the land. Through this all flows of bounty are drawn, for all rain and rainfall descend through the righteous one, as is written: “For God had not caused rain upon the land, and there was no man,” etc. This is the righteous one, through whom all rainfall is drawn, to water the entire face of the ground; for he is the aspect of a river coming out of Eden to water, etc., “and from there it divides,” etc.

He is the aspect of “And a river comes out of Eden to water the garden,” as explained above, for the righteous one waters and saturates the land. Through this all flows of bounty are drawn, for all rain and rainfall descend through the righteous one, as is written: “For God had not caused rain upon the land, and there was no man,” etc. This is the righteous one, through whom all rainfall is drawn, to water the entire face of the ground; for he is the aspect of a river coming out of Eden to water, etc., “and from there it divides,” etc.

pairs.he: וְעַל כֵּן נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק, בִּבְחִינַת וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אֶחָיו, בִּבְחִינַת וְכָל הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה אֶל יוֹסֵף לִשְׁבֹּר כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט הוּא הַמַּשְׁבִּיר וְכוּ׳. כִּי יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הַשַּׁלִּיט, שֶׁהוּא הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הָאַרְבָּעָה יְסוֹדוֹת, שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ בַּיִת וְכוּ׳, (כמבואר במאמר הנ״ל) שֶׁהוּא נָהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת וְכוּ׳, הַמַּשְׁבִּיר, כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הַשְּׂבִיעוֹת וְכָל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת שֶׁכֻּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בְּאַרְבָּעָה יְסוֹדוֹת שֶׁנִּמְשָׁכִין מֵהַצַּדִּיק כַּנַּ״ל.
pairs.en: And therefore all flows of bounty are drawn through the righteous one, in the aspect of “And Yosef sustained his father and his brothers,” in the aspect of “And all the land came to Egypt, to Yosef, to buy grain,” for “Yosef was the ruler; he was the one providing grain,” etc. For Yosef—the ruler, the righteous one of the generation, from whom all four elements are drawn, the head of the house, etc. (as explained in the aforementioned discourse), who is a river coming out of Eden to water [the unnamed object], etc.—is the one providing grain; for from him all satiations and all flows of bounty are drawn, all included in four elements that are drawn from the righteous one, as explained above.

pairs.en: “And God Almighty will grant you mercy.”

pairs.he: עִקַּר הָרַחֲמָנוּת הוּא בִּבְחִינַת ״וְאֵל שַׁדַּי יִתֵּן לָכֶם רַחֲמִים״ ׳לָכֶם׳ דַּיְקָא. הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִתֵּן לָנוּ הָרַחֲמָנוּת, שֶׁיִּמְסֹר אֶת הָרַחֲמָנוּת בְּיָדֵינוּ. כִּי אֶצְלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת, שֶׁגַּם הַחוֹלַאַת הַקָּשָׁה וְכָל הַיִּסּוּרִין הֵם הָרַחֲמָנוּת שֶׁלּוֹ, כִּי בְּוַדַּאי כָּל מַה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה לְהָאָדָם, אֲפִלּוּ יִסּוּרִין קָשִׁים, הַכֹּל הוּא רַק רַחֲמָנוּת.
pairs.en: The essence of compassion is in the aspect of “And God Almighty will grant you mercy”—“you,” specifically. That is, the blessed God will grant us compassion, entrusting compassion into our hands. For with Him, blessed be He, it may be that even severe illness and all sufferings are His compassion. For certainly everything that the blessed God does to a person, even severe sufferings, is all nothing but compassion.
